# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`

{"content":"🚨 **BLOCKING: re-send matcher swallows the opening frame of a second same-name tool call on clean relays (C4/AC3 regression)**

`_matchResentToolCallBlock` is consulted **unconditionally** — `resent ?? _lookupToolCallBlock(...)` means a matcher hit overrides the id/index identity lookup — and its merge condition treats "last block still has empty `partialArgs`" as mergeable. The PR description claims "Merge fires only on an id/index lookup miss — clean relays are unaffected by construction", but the code never checks the lookup, and the ticket's own spec ("when lookup misses **and** the incoming frame has no usable identity match") is not implemented.

**Demonstrated regression** (standard OpenAI-style stream: two parallel same-name calls whose opening frames carry `arguments: ""` — the normal shape; verified with a probe test: **fails on this head, passes on `origin/main`**):

```
chunk1: [{index:0, id:"call_a", function:{name:"bash", arguments:""}}]
chunk2: [{index:1, id:"call_b", function:{name:"bash", arguments:""}}]   ← swallowed
chunk3: [{index:0, function:{arguments:"{\"command\":\"ls\"}"}}]
chunk4: [{index:1, function:{arguments:"{\"command\":\"pwd\"}"}}]        ← creates a nameless/idless block
```

Result on this head: call 2 ends with `id: ""` **and** `name: ""` (unresolvable tool downstream). At the moment call B's opening frame arrives, the last block (A) has empty `partialArgs`, the names match, so `existing.isNotEmpty && !args.startsWith(existing)` is skipped and the frame merges into A — `toolCallBlocksById["call_b"]` is even rebound to A, and index 1 stays unbound, so the later fragment spawns a fresh block with no identity. This violates AC3/C4 ("no behavior change for clean relays"). Secondary hazard of the same ordering bug: a re-sent frame belonging to an *earlier* same-name block (its id/index lookup would HIT) is merged into the *last* block instead, corrupting that block's args.

**Fix** (keeps both new fixtures green):
1. Only consult the matcher when `_lookupToolCallBlock(streamIndex, id)` misses;
2. Require `existing.isNotEmpty` in the matcher — an empty `partialArgs` cannot distinguish "awaiting first fragment" from "genuinely new call".

Also add the missing C3d regression case: two same-name calls with standard empty-args openings (the current C3d test gives call B complete args, which is exactly the shape that dodges the hole).

    "summary": "[BUG] aiin/JoinGonka relay stutter: doubled punctuation in thinking + duplicated tool-call execution",
    "description": "## [BUG] aiin/JoinGonka relay stutter: doubled punctuation in thinking + duplicated tool-call execution

### Product frame

OpenAI-compatible relays (JoinGonka fronting MiniMax-M2.7, observed via provider `aiin`) stutter stream frames: punctuation-only reasoning tokens arrive twice, and a tool-call frame can be re-sent with a freshly generated `id`. The shared adapter must tolerate both — every relay downstream of `streamOpenAICompletions` inherits this.

### Evidence

Session of 2026-10-16 15:53 (owner clip, `aiin/JoinGonka/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M2.7`):

1. **Thinking text has every sentence-punctuation char doubled** — `The user said "Hello"" - a simple greeting.. I should respond in a friendly,, helpful way…`, `I'm Fa,,`, `today??`, `help::`. Letters, `I'm`, `&` are NEVER doubled — punctuation arrives as standalone deltas, and a 1-char overlap/stutter survives the dedupe.
2. **The same bash command executed twice in one turn** — records show `bash {"command":"js hello.js"}` twice, same `startedAt` to the millisecond, different callIds (`chatcmpl-tool-bd624c1dd04fbbc9` / `chatcmpl-tool-9b456367dc7027d2`), one returned clean output, the other `SyntaxError: redeclaration of 'name'` through a different eval path. The model then hallucinated a justification ("I used `qjs` instead") to reconcile the phantom second run — wasted execution plus a confusing ledger.

### Root causes — both in `lib/src/providers/openai_completions.dart`

- **C1 (thinking doubling):** `_dedupeOverlap` — the overlap trim loop is `for (var k = maxK; k >= 2; k--)`. A stutter of exactly 1 char (the punctuation token re-sent) is below the floor and is appended verbatim. ≥2-char stutters are already cleaned (the "Продродололжжж" comment case).
- **C2 (duplicate tool call):** `_ensureToolCallBlock` matches existing blocks only by `streamIndex` / `id`. A re-sent call frame carrying a NEW relay-generated id and no (or another) `index` misses the lookup and spawns a second `ToolCallStreamingBlock` with identical name + arguments → both execute.

### Required capabilities

- **C1 fix:** trim 1-char overlaps too. Ellipsis guard: do NOT trim when the remaining delta starts with the same char again (legit `...` continuations); otherwise a leading single char equal to the current tail is an overlap. Keep the full-snapshot branch and the 64-char window as-is.
- **C2 fix:** in `_ensureToolCallBlock`, when lookup misses and the incoming frame has no usable identity match, check the LAST registered tool-call block of the current message: if its name is non-empty, equals the incoming name, and its `partialArgs` is empty or a prefix of the incoming arguments — treat the frame as a re-send (merge into the existing block, adopt the newer id only if the old one is empty) instead of spawning a block.
- **C3 — regression guards:** unit tests simulating a stuttering relay: (a) reasoning deltas `greeting`, `.`, `.`, ` I should` → thinking contains `greeting. I should`; (b) `...` ellipsis split across deltas survives untrimmed; (c) tool-call frames A(id1, name, args) then B(id2, same name, same args) → ONE block, args correct; (d) two genuinely different calls in one message still produce two blocks.
- **C4 — no behavior change for clean relays:** OpenRouter/DeepSeek/litellm-style clean delta streams must produce byte-identical output (existing adapter tests stay green).

### Test matrix

- `test/providers/openai_completions_dedupe_test.dart` (or the file where `_dedupeOverlap` is covered today): cases C3a–C3d.
- Existing openai-completions adapter tests: unchanged green (C4).

### Platform inventory

- `lib/src/providers/openai_completions.dart` only (shared adapter; `aiin`, openrouter, deepseek and every custom baseUrl route through it). No session/protocol/UI changes. Pure Dart, no new deps.

### Security

No new data flows; all parsing stays on already-received frames.

### Acceptance

- [ ] AC1: stuttering-reasoning fixtures produce clean thinking text (C3a), ellipsis intact (C3b).
- [ ] AC2: re-sent tool-call frame with fresh id does not execute twice (C3c); distinct calls still distinct (C3d).
- [ ] AC3: existing adapter tests untouched and green (C4).
- [ ] AC4: live check against `aiin/JoinGonka/MiniMax-M2.7`: thinking without doubled punctuation; a tool-call turn executes each command exactly once.

+name: android-ndk-preinstall
+description: >-
+  Pre-install the Flutter-pinned Android NDK so Gradle configuration never
+  triggers an on-demand sdkmanager download mid-build. gh-1655: one
+  truncated android-ndk-r28c-linux download ("Error on ZipFile unknown
+  archive" at 33%) red'd the ci.yml build-android leg — and the aggregate
+  Quality gate with it — because AGP's in-configuration auto-install path
+  has NO retry. The NDK version is resolved from the pinned Flutter SDK's
+  own gradle plugin source (the exact value flutter.ndkVersion resolves
+  to — no second pin to drift), the install is skipped when the NDK is
+  already present, and the download itself is bounded-retried — the same
+  hardening the flutter_gemma Android seed carries (gh-1468). Companion
+  guard: test/ci_android_ndk_preinstall_guard_test.dart.
+runs:
+  using: composite
+  steps:
+    - name: Pre-install the Flutter-pinned Android NDK (bounded retry)
+      shell: bash
+      run: |
+        set -euo pipefail
+        # flutter.ndkVersion's single source of truth: the gradle plugin
+        # bundled with the SDK flutter-action installed. app/
+        # build.gradle.kts reads `ndkVersion = flutter.ndkVersion`, so
+        # resolving here can never skew from what AGP requests at
+        # configuration time (a literal pin on either side would break
+        # that coupling — the guard test pins both sides).
+        if [ -n "${FLUTTER_ROOT:-}" ]; then
+          FLUTTER_HOME="$FLUTTER_ROOT"
+        else
+          FLUTTER_BIN="$(command -v flutter || true)"
+          if [ -z "$FLUTTER_BIN" ]; then
+            echo "::error::cannot locate flutter (set FLUTTER_ROOT) — the NDK pre-install resolves the version from the SDK's gradle plugin source"
+            exit 1
+          fi
+          FLUTTER_HOME="$(dirname "$(dirname "$FLUTTER_BIN")")"
+        fi
+        GRADLE_SRC="$FLUTTER_HOME/packages/flutter_tools/gradle/src/main/kotlin/FlutterExtension.kt"
+        NDK_VERSION="$(grep -hoE 'val ndkVersion: String = "[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+"' "$GRADLE_SRC" 2>/dev/null | grep -oE '[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+' | head -1 || true)"
+        if [ -z "$NDK_VERSION" ]; then
+          echo "::error::cannot resolve flutter.ndkVersion from $GRADLE_SRC — the Flutter gradle plugin layout moved; update the extraction in .github/actions/android-ndk-preinstall (and test/ci_android_ndk_preinstall_guard_test.dart) TOGETHER"
+          exit 1
+        fi
+        echo "resolved flutter.ndkVersion = $NDK_VERSION"
+        ANDROID_SDK="${ANDROID_HOME:-/usr/local/lib/android/sdk}"
+        SDKMANAGER="$ANDROID_SDK/cmdline-tools/latest/bin/sdkmanager"
+        if [ ! -x "$SDKMANAGER" ]; then
+          SDKMANAGER="$(command -v sdkmanager || true)"
+        fi
+        if [ -z "$SDKMANAGER" ]; then
+          echo "::error::sdkmanager not found (expected $ANDROID_SDK/cmdline-tools/latest/bin/sdkmanager) — the NDK pre-install needs the Android cmdline-tools"
+          exit 1
+        fi
+        # Idempotence: AGP resolves `ndkVersion` against
+        # $ANDROID_HOME/ndk/<version> — source.properties present means
+        # the NDK is fully installed; skip the download entirely.
+        if [ -f "$ANDROID_SDK/ndk/$NDK_VERSION/source.properties" ]; then
+          echo "NDK $NDK_VERSION already installed — skipping pre-install"
+          exit 0
+        fi
+        # Accept any license the image has not pre-accepted so the
+        # installs below never prompt (|| true: `yes` dies of SIGPIPE by
+        # design once sdkmanager stops reading).
+        yes | "$SDKMANAGER" --licenses > /dev/null || true
+        # gh-1655: Gradle's own auto-install (the same sdkmanager call,
+        # run inside configuration) has no retry — one truncated download
+        # unzips as "Error on ZipFile unknown archive" and the build dies.
+        # Here the same download gets three attempts with backoff.
+        for attempt in 1 2 3; do
+          echo "installing NDK $NDK_VERSION (attempt $attempt/3)"
+          rm -rf "$ANDROID_SDK/ndk/$NDK_VERSION"
+          if "$SDKMANAGER" --install "ndk;$NDK_VERSION"; then
+            echo "NDK $NDK_VERSION installed"
+            exit 0
+          fi
+          echo "::warning::sdkmanager NDK install failed (attempt $attempt/3) — retrying in 10s"
+          sleep 10
+        done
+        echo "::error::NDK $NDK_VERSION install failed after 3 attempts — gh-1655 red'd the leg on a single truncated archive; inspect the sdkmanager output above"
+        exit 1

Frame 1: `{index: 0, id: 'call_a', function: {name: 'bash', arguments: '{"command":"ls"}'}}` (complete args in one frame).
- `_matchResentToolCallBlock`: no tool-call block yet → last=null → null.
- `_ensureToolCallBlock`: lookup(0, 'call_a') → miss → create A. partialArgs = '{"command":"ls"}'.

Frame 2 (second identical call): `{index: 1, id: 'call_b', function: {name: 'bash', arguments: '{"command":"ls"}'}}`.

- `_ensureToolCallBlock`: block = A (resend wins over lookup → lookup(1,'call_b') never consulted → miss not detected).
- `_applyToolCallIdentity(A, frame2)`: A.id is non-empty ('call_a'), so id NOT adopted. A.name non-empty → not updated.

- Result: ONE block. The second identical call is silently swallowed. ToolCallStartEvent for it never fires; index 1/id 'call_b' never registered.

This confirms: a clean relay emitting two identical calls in one message now produces ONE call. This violates C4/AC3 ("no behavior change for clean relays... byte-identical output") and is a real correctness regression (silent dropped tool call). And it contradicts the PR description's claim "Merge fires only on an id/index lookup miss — clean relays are unaffected by construction."

The ticket spec says the resend check should happen "when lookup misses and the incoming frame has no usable identity match". The implementation inverted the order: matcher first, identity lookup second. The fix would be to consult `_matchResentToolCallBlock` only when `_lookupToolCallBlock(streamIndex, id)` misses (and arguably only when the frame carries a genuinely new id with no matching index — per ticket: "a frame whose name equals..." — the PR description itself says "on a lookup miss").

Re-sent frame with fresh id `call_b` and NO index: lookup(null, 'call_b') → toolCallBlocksById['call_b'] → miss (new id never seen) → then matcher → merge. ✓. Re-sent frame with fresh id AND an index (some relays resend with index): the ticket says "carrying a NEW relay-generated id and no (or another) index". If it carried the SAME index → lookup hits → merge via normal path. If it carries ANOTHER index → lookup misses → matcher fires → merge (but then the streamIndex registration: block.streamIndex != null (0) so not overwritten; `toolCallBlocksByIndex[1] = A`? No — the `if (streamIndex != null && block.streamIndex == null)` guard prevents rebinding index 1 to A. Hmm, but then future frames with index 1 would create a new block... messy but that's the stutter case).

So the correct ordering (lookup first, matcher on miss) would fix Scenario A while still fixing the bug. The current implementation is a deviation from the ticket's specified fix.

Is Scenario A realistic enough for BLOCKING? Two identical tool calls in one message: e.g., a model calling `read` twice on the same file with identical args (common when the model wants fresh content — actually identical parallel reads happen), or two identical `grep` calls, or web_search with the same query twice. Models do this occasionally, especially in parallel-tool-call mode. The result: one call silently dropped. This is a correctness bug on clean relays introduced by this PR — exactly the class of regression AC3/C4 was written to prevent. Severity: BLOCKING.

A (index 0, bash) done; B (index 1, bash) streaming with partialArgs '{"comma'. A re-sent A frame arrives: `{index: 0, function: {name: 'bash', arguments: '{"command":"ls"}'}}`.

- `_ensureToolCallBlock`: block = B. Lookup would have routed by index 0 → A. Instead the frame merges into B: toolDelta='{"command":"ls"}' minus prefix '{"comma' → 'nd":"ls"}' appended to B → B.args = '{"command":"ls"}' — corrupted; A loses its resend (fine, A was complete anyway).

So the correct order (lookup first) would route to A, then `resend`-less append: toolDelta='{"command":"ls"}' appended to A's args → A.args doubled ('{"command":"ls"}{"command":"ls"}')! Hmm, so lookup-first alone doesn't fix the stutter for re-sent COMPLETE frames against completed blocks — the suffix trim is keyed on `resend != null`. But wait — if lookup HITS (same index 0), that's the same-id same-index re-send case: the PR's fix as written doesn't trim there either (resend matcher only helps when matched). Actually if lookup hits A and the frame is a full re-send of A's args, old behavior: args doubled. New behavior with lookup-first: still doubled (no trim). Hmm.

The JoinGonka evidence shows a re-sent frame with a FRESH id — i.e. the same call re-sent with a new id right around the same point. blocks.text:
name: android-ndk-preinstall
description: >-
  Pre-install the Flutter-pinned Android NDK so Gradle configuration never
  triggers an on-demand sdkmanager download mid-build. gh-1655: one
  truncated android-ndk-r28c-linux download ("Error on ZipFile unknown
  archive" at 33%) red'd the ci.yml build-android leg — and the aggregate
  Quality gate with it — because AGP's in-configuration auto-install path
  has NO retry. The NDK version is resolved from the pinned Flutter SDK's
  own gradle plugin source (the exact value flutter.ndkVersion resolves
  to — no second pin to drift), the install is skipped when the NDK is
  already present, and the download itself is bounded-retried — the same
  hardening the flutter_gemma Android seed carries (gh-1468). Companion
  guard: test/ci_android_ndk_preinstall_guard_test.dart.
runs:
  using: composite
  steps:
    - name: Pre-install the Flutter-pinned Android NDK (bounded retry)
      shell: bash
      run: |
        set -euo pipefail
        # flutter.ndkVersion's single source of truth: the gradle plugin
        # bundled with the SDK flutter-action installed. app/
        # build.gradle.kts reads `ndkVersion = flutter.ndkVersion`, so
        # resolving here can never skew from what AGP requests at
        # configuration time (a literal pin on either side would break
        # that coupling — the guard test pins both sides).
        if [ -n "${FLUTTER_ROOT:-}" ]; then
          FLUTTER_HOME="$FLUTTER_ROOT"
        else
          FLUTTER_BIN="$(command -v flutter || true)"
          if [ -z "$FLUTTER_BIN" ]; then
            echo "::error::cannot locate flutter (set FLUTTER_ROOT) — the NDK pre-install resolves the version from the SDK's gradle plugin source"
            exit 1
          fi
          FLUTTER_HOME="$(dirname "$(dirname "$FLUTTER_BIN")")"
        fi
        GRADLE_SRC="$FLUTTER_HOME/packages/flutter_tools/gradle/src/main/kotlin/FlutterExtension.kt"
        NDK_VERSION="$(grep -hoE 'val ndkVersion: String = "[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+"' "$GRADLE_SRC" 2>/dev/null | grep -oE '[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+' | head -1 || true)"
        if [ -z "$NDK_VERSION" ]; then
          echo "::error::cannot resolve flutter.ndkVersion from $GRADLE_SRC — the Flutter gradle plugin layout moved; update the extraction in .github/actions/android-ndk-preinstall (and test/ci_android_ndk_preinstall_guard_test.dart) TOGETHER"
          exit 1
        fi
        echo "resolved flutter.ndkVersion = $NDK_VERSION"
        ANDROID_SDK="${ANDROID_HOME:-/usr/local/lib/android/sdk}"
        SDKMANAGER="$ANDROID_SDK/cmdline-tools/latest/bin/sdkmanager"
        if [ ! -x "$SDKMANAGER" ]; then
          SDKMANAGER="$(command -v sdkmanager || true)"
        fi
        if [ -z "$SDKMANAGER" ]; then
          echo "::error::sdkmanager not found (expected $ANDROID_SDK/cmdline-tools/latest/bin/sdkmanager) — the NDK pre-install needs the Android cmdline-tools"
          exit 1
        fi
        # Idempotence: AGP resolves `ndkVersion` against
        # $ANDROID_HOME/ndk/<version> — source.properties present means
        # the NDK is fully installed; skip the download entirely.
        if [ -f "$ANDROID_SDK/ndk/$NDK_VERSION/source.properties" ]; then
          echo "NDK $NDK_VERSION already installed — skipping pre-install"
          exit 0
        fi
        # Accept any license the image has not pre-accepted so the
        # installs below never prompt (|| true: `yes` dies of SIGPIPE by
        # design once sdkmanager stops reading).
        yes | "$SDKMANAGER" --licenses > /dev/null || true
        # gh-1655: Gradle's own auto-install (the same sdkmanager call,
        # run inside configuration) has no retry — one truncated download
        # unzips as "Error on ZipFile unknown archive" and the build dies.
        # Here the same download gets three attempts with backoff.
        for attempt in 1 2 3; do
          echo "installing NDK $NDK_VERSION (attempt $attempt/3)"
          rm -rf "$ANDROID_SDK/ndk/$NDK_VERSION"
          if "$SDKMANAGER" --install "ndk;$NDK_VERSION"; then
            echo "NDK $NDK_VERSION installed"
            exit 0
          fi
          echo "::warning::sdkmanager NDK install failed (attempt $attempt/3) — retrying in 10s"
          sleep 10
        done
        echo "::error::NDK $NDK_VERSION install failed after 3 attempts — gh-1655 red'd the leg on a single truncated archive; inspect the sdkmanager output above"
        exit 1

**Base passes, PR head fails.** This is a definitive, PR-introduced regression on a standard clean-relay stream shape:

- PR head: `call_b` → empty id, empty name.

This is BLOCKING (correctness bug, violates AC3/C4 of the ticket itself).

Now clean up: remove the probe from both places and the worktree. Then run the PR's provider suite to confirm the rest is green, and run the new guard test.

Then finalize findings:

**BLOCKING 1** — `_matchResentToolCallBlock` fires on the standard OpenAI multi-call opening shape (name repeated, empty `partialArgs` on last block, `arguments: ""`) and overrides the id/index lookup, so the second same-name call's opening frame is swallowed → block created later from arg fragments with empty id AND empty name. Demonstrated: probe fails on head, passes on base. Violates ticket AC3/C4 ("existing adapter tests untouched and green" / "no behavior change for clean relays"). Anchor: the `final resend = _matchResentToolCallBlock(rawToolCall);` line or the `resent ?? _lookupToolCallBlock` line in the diff. Fix direction: only consult the matcher when the id/index lookup MISSES and the incoming frame is genuinely identity-less relative to registered blocks (per the ticket's own spec wording: "when lookup misses and the incoming frame has no usable identity match"), and don't merge when the last block has no args yet (an empty `partialArgs` cannot distinguish "awaiting first fragment" from "new call") — or at minimum require `existing.isNotEmpty` in the matcher.

Wait — careful: requiring `existing.isNotEmpty` would break the PR's own C3c test? Let me check: re-sent frame with fresh id, args FULL '{"command":"js hello.js"}', existing after frame 1 = '{"command":"js hello.js"}' — non-empty → still merges. Good, C3c survives. And the empty-existing guard would fix my probe: at call_b's opening, existing='' → no merge → lookup(1,'call_b') → miss → create properly. The re-send case in the wild (evidence) had the block's args fully accumulated → existing non-empty → merge works. So the minimal fix (`existing.isNotEmpty` + lookup-miss gating) preserves the PR's goals and fixes the regression. I'll propose exactly that.

Also check: does the early-return `if (toolDelta.isEmpty) return;` skip the `ToolCallDeltaEvent` — for a swallowed-duplicate frame that's fine.

**IMPORTANT/SUGGESTION items:**

2. **Matcher bypasses identity lookup on hit (deviation from ticket spec)** — Scenario B: a re-sent frame for a non-last block with same name and prefix-matching args merges into the WRONG block, corrupting args. The ticket says the resend check applies only "when lookup misses and the incoming frame has no usable identity match"; the impl applies it always (`resent ?? lookup`). It's really the same root cause as BLOCKING 1 — I'll fold it into the same comment (root cause + both symptoms), keeping one blocking finding. Cleaner.

3. **`_dedupeOverlap` 1-char trim can eat legit single-char deltas** ("soo" + "o" → "soo"; letter triplets "yesss" typed as single-char deltas). Ticket-mandated heuristic; ellipsis guard only protects in-delta repeats. SUGGESTION (document/accept; maybe restrict 1-char trim to punctuation-only deltas — actually the ticket evidence is punctuation; restricting the 1-char trim to punctuation chars would remove the letters-loss class and still fix C1. That's a decent suggestion).

Hmm wait — actually think again about whether the 1-char trim has a WORSE false positive for clean relays: clean relay token split "wait", ".", " Again"? Then '.' appended (text 'wait' doesn't end with '.'). "wait." then " I should". Fine. Legit double punctuation like "?!" split: "really" + "?" + "!" → 'really?!' — second delta '!' — text ends with '?' not '!' → appended ✓. Legit "!!" as separate deltas: "wow" + "!" + "!" → second '!' trimmed → 'wow!' — data loss on clean relay! "Hello!!" is real text. But same accepted tradeoff class as ticket C1. The guard `delta.codeUnitAt(1)==delta.codeUnitAt(0)` doesn't help (delta length 1). I'll keep it as a suggestion (restrict 1-char trim to sentence punctuation `.,;:!?…` — the observed stutter class — or require the delta to be a single punctuation char AND the previous delta to have been punctuation... keep simple: punctuation-restricted 1-char trim). Note: the ticket says "trim 1-char overlaps too" without restricting, so the impl follows the ticket; the false-positive classes are inherent to the ticket spec. SUGGESTION.

The ticket is a bug report, not a strict scope contract; the CI changes are defensible and well-guarded. # AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`

{"content":"🚨 **BLOCKING: re-send matcher swallows the opening frame of a second same-name tool call on clean relays (C4/AC3 regression)**

`_matchResentToolCallBlock` is consulted **unconditionally** — `resent ?? _lookupToolCallBlock(...)` means a matcher hit overrides the id/index identity lookup — and its merge condition treats "last block still has empty `partialArgs`" as mergeable. The PR description claims "Merge fires only on an id/index lookup miss — clean relays are unaffected by construction", but the code never checks the lookup, and the ticket's own spec ("when lookup misses **and** the incoming frame has no usable identity match") is not implemented.

**Demonstrated regression** (standard OpenAI-style stream: two parallel same-name calls whose opening frames carry `arguments: ""` — the normal shape; verified with a probe test: **fails on this head, passes on `origin/main`**):

```
chunk1: [{index:0, id:"call_a", function:{name:"bash", arguments:""}}]
chunk2: [{index:1, id:"call_b", function:{name:"bash", arguments:""}}]   ← swallowed
chunk3: [{index:0, function:{arguments:"{\"command\":\"ls\"}"}}]
chunk4: [{index:1, function:{arguments:"{\"command\":\"pwd\"}"}}]        ← creates a nameless/idless block
```

Result on this head: call 2 ends with `id: ""` **and** `name: ""` (unresolvable tool downstream). At the moment call B's opening frame arrives, the last block (A) has empty `partialArgs`, the names match, so `existing.isNotEmpty && !args.startsWith(existing)` is skipped and the frame merges into A — `toolCallBlocksById["call_b"]` is even rebound to A, and index 1 stays unbound, so the later fragment spawns a fresh block with no identity. This violates AC3/C4 ("no behavior change for clean relays"). Secondary hazard of the same ordering bug: a re-sent frame belonging to an *earlier* same-name block (its id/index lookup would HIT) is merged into the *last* block instead, corrupting that block's args.

**Fix** (keeps both new fixtures green):
1. Only consult the matcher when `_lookupToolCallBlock(streamIndex, id)` misses;

arguments.content:
💡 **SUGGESTION: the 1-char trim also eats legitimate single-char continuations, not only punctuation stutters**

The new `k >= 1` floor trims **any** leading single char equal to the current tail, and the ellipsis guard only fires when the same char repeats *inside* the delta (`delta.length > 1`). So on a clean relay that happens to split tokens as single characters, real text is destroyed:

- `'soo'` + `'o'` → `'soo'` (lost an `o`)
- `'wow'` + `'!'` + `'!'` → `'wow!'`
- `'yes'` + `'s'` + `'s'` → `'yes'`

All the gh-1655 evidence stutters are sentence punctuation (`. , : ; ? !`), and the ticket's C1 concern is exactly that class. Consider restricting the 1-char trim to punctuation-only leading chars (e.g. `const oneCharStutter = '.',',':';'?';!'.contains(delta[0])`) — that keeps the fix targeted at the observed relay defect and makes doubled/tripled letters safe by construction. If you keep the unrestricted trim, at least pin the accepted tradeoff in the doc comment so a future reader doesn't mistake it for a bug.

    "description": "## [BUG] aiin/JoinGonka relay stutter: doubled punctuation in thinking + duplicated tool-call execution

### Product frame

OpenAI-compatible relays (JoinGonka fronting MiniMax-M2.7, observed via provider `aiin`) stutter stream frames: punctuation-only reasoning tokens arrive twice, and a tool-call frame can be re-sent with a freshly generated `id`. The shared adapter must tolerate both — every relay downstream of `streamOpenAICompletions` inherits this.

### Evidence

Session of 2026-10-16 15:53 (owner clip, `aiin/JoinGonka/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M2.7`):

1. **Thinking text has every sentence-punctuation char doubled** — `The user said "Hello"" - a simple greeting.. I should respond in a friendly,, helpful way…`, `I'm Fa,,`, `today??`, `help::`. Letters, `I'm`, `&` are NEVER doubled — punctuation arrives as standalone deltas, and a 1-char overlap/stutter survives the dedupe.
2. **The same bash command executed twice in one turn** — records show `bash {"command":"js hello.js"}` twice, same `startedAt` to the millisecond, different callIds (`chatcmpl-tool-bd624c1dd04fbbc9` / `chatcmpl-tool-9b456367dc7027d2`), one returned clean output, the other `SyntaxError: redeclaration of 'name'` through a different eval path. The model then hallucinated a justification ("I used `qjs` instead") to reconcile the phantom second run — wasted execution plus a confusing ledger.

### Root causes — both in `lib/src/providers/openai_completions.dart`

- **C1 (thinking doubling):** `_dedupeOverlap` — the overlap trim loop is `for (var k = maxK; k >= 2; k--)`. A stutter of exactly 1 char (the punctuation token re-sent) is below the floor and is appended verbatim. ≥2-char stutters are already cleaned (the "Продродололжжж" comment case).
- **C2 (duplicate tool call):** `_ensureToolCallBlock` matches existing blocks only by `streamIndex` / `id`. A re-sent call frame carrying a NEW relay-generated id and no (or another) `index` misses the lookup and spawns a second `ToolCallStreamingBlock` with identical name + arguments → both execute.

### Required capabilities

- **C1 fix:** trim 1-char overlaps too. Ellipsis guard: do NOT trim when the remaining delta starts with the same char again (legit `...` continuations); otherwise a leading single char equal to the current tail is an overlap. Keep the full-snapshot branch and the 64-char window as-is.
- **C2 fix:** in `_ensureToolCallBlock`, when lookup misses and the incoming frame has no usable identity match, check the LAST registered tool-call block of the current message: if its name is non-empty, equals the incoming name, and its `partialArgs` is empty or a prefix of the incoming arguments — treat the frame as a re-send (merge into the existing block, adopt the newer id only if the old one is empty) instead of spawning a block.
- **C3 — regression guards:** unit tests simulating a stuttering relay: (a) reasoning deltas `greeting`, `.`, `.`, ` I should` → thinking contains `greeting. I should`; (b) `...` ellipsis split across deltas survives untrimmed; (c) tool-call frames A(id1, name, args) then B(id2, same name, same args) → ONE block, args correct; (d) two genuinely different calls in one message still produce two blocks.
- **C4 — no behavior change for clean relays:** OpenRouter/DeepSeek/litellm-style clean delta streams must produce byte-identical output (existing adapter tests stay green).

### Test matrix

- `test/providers/openai_completions_dedupe_test.dart` (or the file where `_dedupeOverlap` is covered today): cases C3a–C3d.
- Existing openai-completions adapter tests: unchanged green (C4).

### Platform inventory

- `lib/src/providers/openai_completions.dart` only (shared adapter; `aiin`, openrouter, deepseek and every custom baseUrl route through it). No session/protocol/UI changes. Pure Dart, no new deps.

### Security

No new data flows; all parsing stays on already-received frames.

- [ ] AC1: stuttering-reasoning fixtures produce clean thinking text (C3a), ellipsis intact (C3b).
- [ ] AC2: re-sent tool-call frame with fresh id does not execute twice (C3c); distinct calls still distinct (C3d).
- [ ] AC3: existing adapter tests untouched and green (C4).

name: android-ndk-preinstall
description: >-
  Pre-install the Flutter-pinned Android NDK so Gradle configuration never
  triggers an on-demand sdkmanager download mid-build. gh-1655: one
  truncated android-ndk-r28c-linux download ("Error on ZipFile unknown
  archive" at 33%) red'd the ci.yml build-android leg — and the aggregate
  Quality gate with it — because AGP's in-configuration auto-install path
  has NO retry. The NDK version is resolved from the pinned Flutter SDK's
  own gradle plugin source (the exact value flutter.ndkVersion resolves
  to — no second pin to drift), the install is skipped when the NDK is
  already present, and the download itself is bounded-retried — the same
  hardening the flutter_gemma Android seed carries (gh-1468). Companion
  guard: test/ci_android_ndk_preinstall_guard_test.dart.
runs:
  using: composite
  steps:
    - name: Pre-install the Flutter-pinned Android NDK (bounded retry)
      shell: bash
      run: |
        set -euo pipefail
        # flutter.ndkVersion's single source of truth: the gradle plugin
        # bundled with the SDK flutter-action installed. app/
        # build.gradle.kts reads `ndkVersion = flutter.ndkVersion`, so
        # resolving here can never skew from what AGP requests at
        # configuration time (a literal pin on either side would break
        # that coupling — the guard test pins both sides).
        if [ -n "${FLUTTER_ROOT:-}" ]; then
          FLUTTER_HOME="$FLUTTER_ROOT"
        else
          FLUTTER_BIN="$(command -v flutter || true)"
          if [ -z "$FLUTTER_BIN" ]; then
            echo "::error::cannot locate flutter (set FLUTTER_ROOT) — the NDK pre-install resolves the version from the SDK's gradle plugin source"
            exit 1
          fi
          FLUTTER_HOME="$(dirname "$(dirname "$FLUTTER_BIN")")"
        fi
        GRADLE_SRC="$FLUTTER_HOME/packages/flutter_tools/gradle/src/main/kotlin/FlutterExtension.kt"
        NDK_VERSION="$(grep -hoE 'val ndkVersion: String = "[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+"' "$GRADLE_SRC" 2>/dev/null | grep -oE '[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+' | head -1 || true)"
        if [ -z "$NDK_VERSION" ]; then
          echo "::error::cannot resolve flutter.ndkVersion from $GRADLE_SRC — the Flutter gradle plugin layout moved; update the extraction in .github/actions/android-ndk-preinstall (and test/ci_android_ndk_preinstall_guard_test.dart) TOGETHER"
          exit 1
        fi
        echo "resolved flutter.ndkVersion = $NDK_VERSION"
        ANDROID_SDK="${ANDROID_HOME:-/usr/local/lib/android/sdk}"
        SDKMANAGER="$ANDROID_SDK/cmdline-tools/latest/bin/sdkmanager"
        if [ ! -x "$SDKMANAGER" ]; then
          SDKMANAGER="$(command -v sdkmanager || true)"
        fi
        if [ -z "$SDKMANAGER" ]; then
          echo "::error::sdkmanager not found (expected $ANDROID_SDK/cmdline-tools/latest/bin/sdkmanager) — the NDK pre-install needs the Android cmdline-tools"
          exit 1
        fi
        # Idempotence: AGP resolves `ndkVersion` against
        # $ANDROID_HOME/ndk/<version> — source.properties present means
        # the NDK is fully installed; skip the download entirely.
        if [ -f "$ANDROID_SDK/ndk/$NDK_VERSION/source.properties" ]; then
          echo "NDK $NDK_VERSION already installed — skipping pre-install"
          exit 0
        fi
        # Accept any license the image has not pre-accepted so the
        # installs below never prompt (|| true: `yes` dies of SIGPIPE by
        # design once sdkmanager stops reading).
        yes | "$SDKMANAGER" --licenses > /dev/null || true
        # gh-1655: Gradle's own auto-install (the same sdkmanager call,
        # run inside configuration) has no retry — one truncated download
        # unzips as "Error on ZipFile unknown archive" and the build dies.
        # Here the same download gets three attempts with backoff.
        for attempt in 1 2 3; do
          echo "installing NDK $NDK_VERSION (attempt $attempt/3)"
          rm -rf "$ANDROID_SDK/ndk/$NDK_VERSION"
          if "$SDKMANAGER" --install "ndk;$NDK_VERSION"; then
            echo "NDK $NDK_VERSION installed"
            exit 0
          fi
          echo "::warning::sdkmanager NDK install failed (attempt $attempt/3) — retrying in 10s"
          sleep 10
        done
        echo "::error::NDK $NDK_VERSION install failed after 3 attempts — gh-1655 red'd the leg on a single truncated archive; inspect the sdkmanager output above"
        exit 1

The ticket's own spec would swallow the second call's opening frame. BUT the ticket spec adds the precondition: "when lookup misses **and the incoming frame has no usable identity match**". A frame WITH `index: 1` where index 1 is unbound — is that "no usable identity match"? The lookup misses → matcher applies. Hmm. So the ticket spec itself would do the merge in Scenario D.

Scenario B (re-sent frame for a non-last block with same name + prefix-args): lookup would hit the right block (index 0 → A), but the impl merges into B (last). The ticket says the matcher applies only on lookup miss. This is a real deviation.

Let me construct a concrete harmful case for the impl-vs-spec deviation that is REALISTIC:

A stuttering relay re-sends frames — that's the whole premise. Evidence shows the relay re-sent a tool-call frame with a fresh id. What if the relay re-sends a frame carrying the OLD id (id+name+args complete) AFTER a second call B has started? Now clean up: remove the probe from both places and the worktree. Then run the PR's provider suite to confirm the rest is green, and run the new guard test.

Then finalize findings:

**BLOCKING 1** — `_matchResentToolCallBlock` fires on the standard OpenAI multi-call opening shape (name repeated, empty `partialArgs` on last block, `arguments: ""`) and overrides the id/index lookup, so the second same-name call's opening frame is swallowed → block created later from arg fragments with empty id AND empty name. Demonstrated: probe fails on head, passes on base. Violates ticket AC3/C4 ("existing adapter tests untouched and green" / "no behavior change for clean relays"). Anchor: the `final resend = _matchResentToolCallBlock(rawToolCall);` line or the `resent ?? _lookupToolCallBlock` line in the diff. Fix direction: only consult the matcher when the id/index lookup MISSES and the incoming frame is genuinely identity-less relative to registered blocks (per the ticket's own spec wording: "when lookup misses and the incoming frame has no usable identity match"), and don't merge when the last block has no args yet (an empty `partialArgs` cannot distinguish "awaiting first fragment" from "new call") — or at minimum require `existing.isNotEmpty` in the matcher.

Wait — careful: requiring `existing.isNotEmpty` would break the PR's own C3c test? Let me check: re-sent frame with fresh id, args FULL '{"command":"js hello.js"}', existing after frame 1 = '{"command":"js hello.js"}' — non-empty → still merges. Good, C3c survives. And the empty-existing guard would fix my probe: at call_b's opening, existing='' → no merge → lookup(1,'call_b') → miss → create properly. The re-send case in the wild (evidence) had the block's args fully accumulated → existing non-empty → merge works. So the minimal fix (`existing.isNotEmpty` + lookup-miss gating) preserves the PR's goals and fixes the regression. I'll propose exactly that.

Also check: does the early-return `if (toolDelta.isEmpty) return;` skip the `ToolCallDeltaEvent` — for a swallowed-duplicate frame that's fine.

The ticket says the resend check applies only "when lookup misses and the incoming frame has no usable identity match"; the impl applies it always (`resent ?? lookup`). It's really the same root cause as BLOCKING 1 — I'll fold it into the same comment (root cause + both symptoms), keeping one blocking finding. Cleaner.

Then '.' appended (text 'wait' doesn't end with '.'). "wait." then " I should". Fine. Legit double punctuation like "?!" split: "really" + "?" + "!" → 'really?!' — second delta '!' — text ends with '?' not '!' → appended ✓. Legit "!!" as separate deltas: "wow" + "!" + "!" → second '!' trimmed → 'wow!' — data loss on clean relay! "Hello!!" is real text. But same accepted tradeoff class as ticket C1. # AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`

{"content":"🚨 **BLOCKING: re-send matcher swallows the opening frame of a second same-name tool call on clean relays (C4/AC3 regression)**

`_matchResentToolCallBlock` is consulted **unconditionally** — `resent ?? _lookupToolCallBlock(...)` means a matcher hit overrides the id/index identity lookup — and its merge condition treats "last block still has empty `partialArgs`" as mergeable. The PR description claims "Merge fires only on an id/index lookup miss — clean relays are unaffected by construction", but the code never checks the lookup, and the ticket's own spec ("when lookup misses **and** the incoming frame has no usable identity match") is not implemented.

**Demonstrated regression** (standard OpenAI-style stream: two parallel same-name calls whose opening frames carry `arguments: ""` — the normal shape; verified with a probe test: **fails on this head, passes on `origin/main`**):

```
chunk1: [{index:0, id:"call_a", function:{name:"bash", arguments:""}}]
chunk2: [{index:1, id:"call_b", function:{name:"bash", arguments:""}}]   ← swallowed
chunk3: [{index:0, function:{arguments:"{\"command\":\"ls\"}"}}]
chunk4: [{index:1, function:{arguments:"{\"command\":\"pwd\"}"}}]        ← creates a nameless/idless block
```

Result on this head: call 2 ends with `id: ""` **and** `name: ""` (unresolvable tool downstream). At the moment call B's opening frame arrives, the last block (A) has empty `partialArgs`, the names match, so `existing.isNotEmpty && !args.startsWith(existing)` is skipped and the frame merges into A — `toolCallBlocksById["call_b"]` is even rebound to A, and index 1 stays unbound, so the later fragment spawns a fresh block with no identity. This violates AC3/C4 ("no behavior change for clean relays"). Secondary hazard of the same ordering bug: a re-sent frame belonging to an *earlier* same-name block (its id/index lookup would HIT) is merged into the *last* block instead, corrupting that block's args.

**Fix** (keeps both new fixtures green):
1. Only consult the matcher when `_lookupToolCallBlock(streamIndex, id)` misses;
2. Require `existing.isNotEmpty` in the matcher — an empty `partialArgs` cannot distinguish "awaiting first fragment" from "genuinely new call".

Also add the missing C3d regression case: two same-name calls with standard empty-args openings (the current C3d test gives call B complete args, which is exactly the shape that dodges the hole).

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: the 1-char trim also eats legitimate single-char continuations, not only punctuation stutters**

The new `k >= 1` floor trims **any** leading single char equal to the current tail, and the ellipsis guard only fires when the same char repeats *inside* the delta (`delta.length > 1`). So on a clean relay that happens to split tokens as single characters, real text is destroyed:

- `'wow'` + `'!'` + `'!'` → `'wow!'`
- `'yes'` + `'s'` + `'s'` → `'yes'`

All the gh-1655 evidence stutters are sentence punctuation (`. , : ; ? !`), and the ticket's C1 concern is exactly that class. Consider restricting the 1-char trim to punctuation-only leading chars (e.g. `const oneCharStutter = '.',',':';'?';!'.contains(delta[0])`) — that keeps the fix targeted at the observed relay defect and makes doubled/tripled letters safe by construction. If you keep the unrestricted trim, at least pin the accepted tradeoff in the doc comment so a future reader doesn't mistake it for a bug.

This confirms: a clean relay emitting two identical calls in one message now produces ONE call. And it contradicts the PR description's claim "Merge fires only on an id/index lookup miss — clean relays are unaffected by construction."

blocks.text:
name: android-ndk-preinstall
description: >-
  Pre-install the Flutter-pinned Android NDK so Gradle configuration never
  triggers an on-demand sdkmanager download mid-build. gh-1655: one
  truncated android-ndk-r28c-linux download ("Error on ZipFile unknown
  archive" at 33%) red'd the ci.yml build-android leg — and the aggregate
  Quality gate with it — because AGP's in-configuration auto-install path
  has NO retry. The NDK version is resolved from the pinned Flutter SDK's
  own gradle plugin source (the exact value flutter.ndkVersion resolves
  to — no second pin to drift), the install is skipped when the NDK is
  already present, and the download itself is bounded-retried — the same
  hardening the flutter_gemma Android seed carries (gh-1468). Companion
  guard: test/ci_android_ndk_preinstall_guard_test.dart.
runs:
  using: composite
  steps:
    - name: Pre-install the Flutter-pinned Android NDK (bounded retry)
      shell: bash
      run: |
        set -euo pipefail
        # flutter.ndkVersion's single source of truth: the gradle plugin
        # bundled with the SDK flutter-action installed. app/
        # build.gradle.kts reads `ndkVersion = flutter.ndkVersion`, so
        # resolving here can never skew from what AGP requests at
        # configuration time (a literal pin on either side would break
        # that coupling — the guard test pins both sides).
        if [ -n "${FLUTTER_ROOT:-}" ]; then
          FLUTTER_HOME="$FLUTTER_ROOT"
        else
          FLUTTER_BIN="$(command -v flutter || true)"
          if [ -z "$FLUTTER_BIN" ]; then
            echo "::error::cannot locate flutter (set FLUTTER_ROOT) — the NDK pre-install resolves the version from the SDK's gradle plugin source"
            exit 1
          fi
          FLUTTER_HOME="$(dirname "$(dirname "$FLUTTER_BIN")")"
        fi
        GRADLE_SRC="$FLUTTER_HOME/packages/flutter_tools/gradle/src/main/kotlin/FlutterExtension.kt"
        NDK_VERSION="$(grep -hoE 'val ndkVersion: String = "[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+"' "$GRADLE_SRC" 2>/dev/null | grep -oE '[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+' | head -1 || true)"
        if [ -z "$NDK_VERSION" ]; then
          echo "::error::cannot resolve flutter.ndkVersion from $GRADLE_SRC — the Flutter gradle plugin layout moved; update the extraction in .github/actions/android-ndk-preinstall (and test/ci_android_ndk_preinstall_guard_test.dart) TOGETHER"
          exit 1
        fi
        echo "resolved flutter.ndkVersion = $NDK_VERSION"
        ANDROID_SDK="${ANDROID_HOME:-/usr/local/lib/android/sdk}"
        SDKMANAGER="$ANDROID_SDK/cmdline-tools/latest/bin/sdkmanager"
        if [ ! -x "$SDKMANAGER" ]; then
          SDKMANAGER="$(command -v sdkmanager || true)"
        fi
        if [ -z "$SDKMANAGER" ]; then
          echo "::error::sdkmanager not found (expected $ANDROID_SDK/cmdline-tools/latest/bin/sdkmanager) — the NDK pre-install needs the Android cmdline-tools"
          exit 1
        fi
        # Idempotence: AGP resolves `ndkVersion` against
        # $ANDROID_HOME/ndk/<version> — source.properties present means
        # the NDK is fully installed; skip the download entirely.
        if [ -f "$ANDROID_SDK/ndk/$NDK_VERSION/source.properties" ]; then
          echo "NDK $NDK_VERSION already installed — skipping pre-install"
          exit 0
        fi
        # Accept any license the image has not pre-accepted so the
        # installs below never prompt (|| true: `yes` dies of SIGPIPE by
        # design once sdkmanager stops reading).
        yes | "$SDKMANAGER" --licenses > /dev/null || true
        # gh-1655: Gradle's own auto-install (the same sdkmanager call,
        # run inside configuration) has no retry — one truncated download
        # unzips as "Error on ZipFile unknown archive" and the build dies.
        # Here the same download gets three attempts with backoff.
        for attempt in 1 2 3; do
          echo "installing NDK $NDK_VERSION (attempt $attempt/3)"
          rm -rf "$ANDROID_SDK/ndk/$NDK_VERSION"
          if "$SDKMANAGER" --install "ndk;$NDK_VERSION"; then
            echo "NDK $NDK_VERSION installed"
            exit 0
          fi
          echo "::warning::sdkmanager NDK install failed (attempt $attempt/3) — retrying in 10s"
          sleep 10
        done
        echo "::error::NDK $NDK_VERSION install failed after 3 attempts — gh-1655 red'd the leg on a single truncated archive; inspect the sdkmanager output above"
        exit 1

**CONFIRMED — the regression is real and demonstrable:**

On a clean OpenAI-style relay streaming two parallel same-name tool calls with the standard opening shape (`arguments: ""`):
- `call_b` loses its id (empty) AND its name (empty) — the second call's opening frame is swallowed as a "re-send" and merged into `call_a`.
- `end id= name= args={command: pwd}` — the second tool call would be emitted with an empty name → unresolvable tool downstream.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`

name: android-ndk-preinstall
description: >-
  Pre-install the Flutter-pinned Android NDK so Gradle configuration never
  triggers an on-demand sdkmanager download mid-build. gh-1655: one
  truncated android-ndk-r28c-linux download ("Error on ZipFile unknown
  archive" at 33%) red'd the ci.yml build-android leg — and the aggregate
  Quality gate with it — because AGP's in-configuration auto-install path
  has NO retry. The NDK version is resolved from the pinned Flutter SDK's
  own gradle plugin source (the exact value flutter.ndkVersion resolves
  to — no second pin to drift), the install is skipped when the NDK is
  already present, and the download itself is bounded-retried — the same
  hardening the flutter_gemma Android seed carries (gh-1468). Companion
  guard: test/ci_android_ndk_preinstall_guard_test.dart.
runs:
  using: composite
  steps:
    - name: Pre-install the Flutter-pinned Android NDK (bounded retry)
      shell: bash
      run: |
        set -euo pipefail
        # flutter.ndkVersion's single source of truth: the gradle plugin
        # bundled with the SDK flutter-action installed. app/
        # build.gradle.kts reads `ndkVersion = flutter.ndkVersion`, so
        # resolving here can never skew from what AGP requests at
        # configuration time (a literal pin on either side would break
        # that coupling — the guard test pins both sides).
        if [ -n "${FLUTTER_ROOT:-}" ]; then
          FLUTTER_HOME="$FLUTTER_ROOT"
        else
          FLUTTER_BIN="$(command -v flutter || true)"
          if [ -z "$FLUTTER_BIN" ]; then
            echo "::error::cannot locate flutter (set FLUTTER_ROOT) — the NDK pre-install resolves the version from the SDK's gradle plugin source"
            exit 1
          fi
          FLUTTER_HOME="$(dirname "$(dirname "$FLUTTER_BIN")")"
        fi
        GRADLE_SRC="$FLUTTER_HOME/packages/flutter_tools/gradle/src/main/kotlin/FlutterExtension.kt"
        NDK_VERSION="$(grep -hoE 'val ndkVersion: String = "[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+"' "$GRADLE_SRC" 2>/dev/null | grep -oE '[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+' | head -1 || true)"
        if [ -z "$NDK_VERSION" ]; then
          echo "::error::cannot resolve flutter.ndkVersion from $GRADLE_SRC — the Flutter gradle plugin layout moved; update the extraction in .github/actions/android-ndk-preinstall (and test/ci_android_ndk_preinstall_guard_test.dart) TOGETHER"
          exit 1
        fi
        echo "resolved flutter.ndkVersion = $NDK_VERSION"
        ANDROID_SDK="${ANDROID_HOME:-/usr/local/lib/android/sdk}"
        SDKMANAGER="$ANDROID_SDK/cmdline-tools/latest/bin/sdkmanager"
        if [ ! -x "$SDKMANAGER" ]; then
          SDKMANAGER="$(command -v sdkmanager || true)"
        fi
        if [ -z "$SDKMANAGER" ]; then
          echo "::error::sdkmanager not found (expected $ANDROID_SDK/cmdline-tools/latest/bin/sdkmanager) — the NDK pre-install needs the Android cmdline-tools"
          exit 1
        fi
        # Idempotence: AGP resolves `ndkVersion` against
        # $ANDROID_HOME/ndk/<version> — source.properties present means
        # the NDK is fully installed; skip the download entirely.
        if [ -f "$ANDROID_SDK/ndk/$NDK_VERSION/source.properties" ]; then
          echo "NDK $NDK_VERSION already installed — skipping pre-install"
          exit 0
        fi
        # Accept any license the image has not pre-accepted so the
        # installs below never prompt (|| true: `yes` dies of SIGPIPE by
        # design once sdkmanager stops reading).
        yes | "$SDKMANAGER" --licenses > /dev/null || true
        # gh-1655: Gradle's own auto-install (the same sdkmanager call,
        # run inside configuration) has no retry — one truncated download
        # unzips as "Error on ZipFile unknown archive" and the build dies.
        # Here the same download gets three attempts with backoff.
        for attempt in 1 2 3; do
          echo "installing NDK $NDK_VERSION (attempt $attempt/3)"
          rm -rf "$ANDROID_SDK/ndk/$NDK_VERSION"
          if "$SDKMANAGER" --install "ndk;$NDK_VERSION"; then
            echo "NDK $NDK_VERSION installed"
            exit 0
          fi
          echo "::warning::sdkmanager NDK install failed (attempt $attempt/3) — retrying in 10s"
          sleep 10
        done
        echo "::error::NDK $NDK_VERSION install failed after 3 attempts — gh-1655 red'd the leg on a single truncated archive; inspect the sdkmanager output above"
        exit 1

Hmm — so the spec-order has its own bug (no dedupe on lookup-hit re-sends), and the impl "fixed" it bypassing lookup — at the cost of misrouting.

**Case 1 (spec-accepted ambiguity):** two identical calls → one block. Ticket C3c mandates this. Not a finding (or a suggestion noting the ambiguity risk — actually I shouldn't even suggest against spec'd behavior; skip, or fold into a note).

**Case 2 (impl deviation, realistic):** sequential different calls, same name, where call 2's opening frame has `arguments: ""` (standard OpenAI opening shape) — matcher matches because `existing` empty... wait no: existing = LAST block's partialArgs. Call 1 completed with args '{"command":"ls"}' (non-empty). Call 2 opening: args='' → `existing.isNotEmpty && !args.startsWith(existing)` → ''.startsWith('{"command":"ls"}') = false → return null. The dangerous sub-case: call 1's opening frame is name-only/empty-args AND call 2's opening frame arrives before call 1's args stream — i.e., both openings in one chunk (parallel calls in one delta array) or back-to-back. What does the session do with an empty-name tool call at finish? Need to check `_finish`/pushBlockEndEvent — the tool call would be emitted with name '' — the agent would fail to resolve the tool. That's a real corruption.

How realistic is "two same-name calls whose openings both carry empty args before any args fragment"? OpenAI's actual streaming: each tool_calls entry arrives in its own chunk, opening chunk has id+name+arguments:"" — yes, OpenAI genuinely sends `"arguments": ""` in the opening chunk (their reference streams do). Two parallel same-name calls: chunk sequence = [open A(args "")], [open B(args "")], [frag A], [frag A], [frag B], [frag B]... — interleaved, actually OpenAI streams call A's args fully then call B's (per index). So: open A (''), open B ('') back-to-back → B's opening swallowed (matcher: last=A, name equal, existing='' → match!). Then A's fragments route by index 0 → A. Then B's fragments `{index:1, args:'{"command":"pwd"}'}` → lookup(1) miss → B created nameless/idless. FINAL: B has empty id AND empty name → downstream tool resolution breaks (ToolCall with name '').

At B's swallowed opening: `_ensureToolCallBlock(frame B, resend=A)`: block=A; `if (streamIndex != null && block.streamIndex == null)` — A.streamIndex=0, not null → skip → index 1 NOT bound. id 'b' → toolCallBlocksById['b'] = A (WRONG but not consulted later since fragment has no id). So lookup(1) → null → create B(id:'', name:'', streamIndex:1). ToolCallStartEvent for B pushed late. args appended. Final: 2 blocks — A fine, B with id='' name='' args correct. ToolCallEndEvent for B → tool call with empty name → the harness would try to execute tool '' → error, or the model transcript gets a nameless call.

For DeepSeek/OpenRouter variants, yes the opening frame typically has `"arguments":""` or the first fragment. Some providers put the first fragment immediately. If the opening has a non-empty first fragment, existing='' → match still fires (existing empty → no prefix check!) — `if (existing.isNotEmpty && !args.startsWith(existing))` — existing='' → condition false → MATCH regardless of args! So ANY same-name call B whose opening frame arrives while last block A has NO args yet gets merged. A has no args yet = A's opening frame just arrived (name+id only, or name+empty args). This is EXACTLY the standard shape of two parallel same-name tool…

**Base passes, PR head fails.** This is a definitive, PR-introduced regression on a standard clean-relay stream shape:

- PR head: `call_b` → empty id, empty name.

This is BLOCKING (correctness bug, violates AC3/C4 of the ticket itself).

Note the base commit: 8659b8247c — hmm, that's `origin/main` tip. The PR diff was computed `origin/main...HEAD`. Good, consistent.

Now clean up: remove the probe from both places and the worktree. Then run the PR's provider suite to confirm the rest is green, and run the new guard test.

Then finalize findings:

**BLOCKING 1** — `_matchResentToolCallBlock` fires on the standard OpenAI multi-call opening shape (name repeated, empty `partialArgs` on last block, `arguments: ""`) and overrides the id/index lookup, so the second same-name call's opening frame is swallowed → block created later from arg fragments with empty id AND empty name. Demonstrated: probe fails on head, passes on base. Violates ticket AC3/C4 ("existing adapter tests untouched and green" / "no behavior change for clean relays"). Anchor: the `final resend = _matchResentToolCallBlock(rawToolCall);` line or the `resent ?? _lookupToolCallBlock` line in the diff. Fix direction: only consult the matcher when the id/index lookup MISSES and the incoming frame is genuinely identity-less relative to registered blocks (per the ticket's own spec wording: "when lookup misses and the incoming frame has no usable identity match"), and don't merge when the last block has no args yet (an empty `partialArgs` cannot distinguish "awaiting first fragment" from "new call") — or at minimum require `existing.isNotEmpty` in the matcher.

Wait — careful: requiring `existing.isNotEmpty` would break the PR's own C3c test? Let me check: re-sent frame with fresh id, args FULL '{"command":"js hello.js"}', existing after frame 1 = '{"command":"js hello.js"}' — non-empty → still merges. Good, C3c survives. And the empty-existing guard would fix my probe: at call_b's opening, existing='' → no merge → lookup(1,'call_b') → miss → create properly. The re-send case in the wild (evidence) had the block's args fully accumulated → existing non-empty → merge works. So the minimal fix (`existing.isNotEmpty` + lookup-miss gating) preserves the PR's goals and fixes the regression. I'll propose exactly that.

Also check: does the early-return `if (toolDelta.isEmpty) return;` skip the `ToolCallDeltaEvent` — for a swallowed-duplicate frame that's fine.

**IMPORTANT/SUGGESTION items:**

2. **Matcher bypasses identity lookup on hit (deviation from ticket spec)** — Scenario B: a re-sent frame for a non-last block with same name and prefix-matching args merges into the WRONG block, corrupting args. The ticket says the resend check applies only "when lookup misses and the incoming frame has no usable identity match"; the impl applies it always (`resent ?? lookup`). It's really the same root cause as BLOCKING 1 — I'll fold it into the same comment (root cause + both symptoms), keeping one blocking finding. Cleaner.

3. **`_dedupeOverlap` 1-char trim can eat legit single-char deltas** ("soo" + "o" → "soo"; letter triplets "yesss" typed as single-char deltas). Ticket-mandated heuristic; ellipsis guard only protects in-delta repeats. SUGGESTION (document/accept; maybe restrict 1-char trim to punctuation-only deltas — actually the ticket evidence is punctuation; restricting the 1-char trim to punctuation chars would remove the letters-loss class and still fix C1. That's a decent suggestion).

Hmm wait — actually think again about whether the 1-char trim has a WORSE false positive for clean relays: clean relay token split "wait", ".", " Again"? Then '.' appended (text 'wait' doesn't end with '.'). "wait." then " I should". Fine. Legit double punctuation like "?!" split: "really" + "?" + "!" → 'really?!' — second delta '!' — text ends with '?' not '!' → appended ✓. Legit "!!" as separate deltas: "wow" + "!" + "!" → second '!' trimmed → 'wow!' — data loss on clean relay! "Hello!!" is real text. But same accepted tradeoff class as ticket C1. The guard `delta.codeUnitAt(1)==delta.codeUnitAt(0)` doesn't help (delta length 1). I'll keep it as a suggestion (restrict 1-char trim to sentence punctuation `.,;:!?…` — the observed stutter class — or require the delta to be a single punctuation char AND the previous delta to have been punctuation... keep simple: punctuation-restricted 1-char trim). Note: the ticket says "trim 1-char overlaps too" without restricting, so the impl follows the ticket; the false-positive classes are inherent to the ticket spec. SUGGESTION.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
