{"content":"🚨 **BLOCKING: re-send matcher swallows the opening frame of a second same-name tool call on clean relays (C4/AC3 regression)**

`_matchResentToolCallBlock` is consulted **unconditionally** — `resent ?? _lookupToolCallBlock(...)` means a matcher hit overrides the id/index identity lookup — and its merge condition treats "last block still has empty `partialArgs`" as mergeable. The PR description claims "Merge fires only on an id/index lookup miss — clean relays are unaffected by construction", but the code never checks the lookup, and the ticket's own spec ("when lookup misses **and** the incoming frame has no usable identity match") is not implemented.

**Demonstrated regression** (standard OpenAI-style stream: two parallel same-name calls whose opening frames carry `arguments: ""` — the normal shape; verified with a probe test: **fails on this head, passes on `origin/main`**):

```
chunk1: [{index:0, id:"call_a", function:{name:"bash", arguments:""}}]
chunk2: [{index:1, id:"call_b", function:{name:"bash", arguments:""}}]   ← swallowed
chunk3: [{index:0, function:{arguments:"{\"command\":\"ls\"}"}}]
chunk4: [{index:1, function:{arguments:"{\"command\":\"pwd\"}"}}]        ← creates a nameless/idless block
```

Result on this head: call 2 ends with `id: ""` **and** `name: ""` (unresolvable tool downstream). At the moment call B's opening frame arrives, the last block (A) has empty `partialArgs`, the names match, so `existing.isNotEmpty && !args.startsWith(existing)` is skipped and the frame merges into A — `toolCallBlocksById["call_b"]` is even rebound to A, and index 1 stays unbound, so the later fragment spawns a fresh block with no identity. This violates AC3/C4 ("no behavior change for clean relays"). Secondary hazard of the same ordering bug: a re-sent frame belonging to an *earlier* same-name block (its id/index lookup would HIT) is merged into the *last* block instead, corrupting that block's args.

**Fix** (keeps both new fixtures green):
1. Only consult the matcher when `_lookupToolCallBlock(streamIndex, id)` misses;
2. Require `existing.isNotEmpty` in the matcher — an empty `partialArgs` cannot distinguish "awaiting first fragment" from "genuinely new call".

Also add the missing C3d regression case: two same-name calls with standard empty-args openings (the current C3d test gives call B complete args, which is exactly the shape that dodges the hole).

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: the 1-char trim also eats legitimate single-char continuations, not only punctuation stutters**

The new `k >= 1` floor trims **any** leading single char equal to the current tail, and the ellipsis guard only fires when the same char repeats *inside* the delta (`delta.length > 1`). So on a clean relay that happens to split tokens as single characters, real text is destroyed:

- `'soo'` + `'o'` → `'soo'` (lost an `o`)
- `'wow'` + `'!'` + `'!'` → `'wow!'`
- `'yes'` + `'s'` + `'s'` → `'yes'`

All the gh-1655 evidence stutters are sentence punctuation (`. , : ; ? !`), and the ticket's C1 concern is exactly that class. Consider restricting the 1-char trim to punctuation-only leading chars (e.g. `const oneCharStutter = '.',',':';'?';!'.contains(delta[0])`) — that keeps the fix targeted at the observed relay defect and makes doubled/tripled letters safe by construction. If you keep the unrestricted trim, at least pin the accepted tradeoff in the doc comment so a future reader doesn't mistake it for a bug.

blocks.text:
name: android-ndk-preinstall
description: >-
  Pre-install the Flutter-pinned Android NDK so Gradle configuration never
  triggers an on-demand sdkmanager download mid-build. gh-1655: one
  truncated android-ndk-r28c-linux download ("Error on ZipFile unknown
  archive" at 33%) red'd the ci.yml build-android leg — and the aggregate
  Quality gate with it — because AGP's in-configuration auto-install path
  has NO retry. The NDK version is resolved from the pinned Flutter SDK's
  own gradle plugin source (the exact value flutter.ndkVersion resolves
  to — no second pin to drift), the install is skipped when the NDK is
  already present, and the download itself is bounded-retried — the same
  hardening the flutter_gemma Android seed carries (gh-1468). Companion
  guard: test/ci_android_ndk_preinstall_guard_test.dart.
runs:
  using: composite
  steps:
    - name: Pre-install the Flutter-pinned Android NDK (bounded retry)
      shell: bash
      run: |
        set -euo pipefail
        # flutter.ndkVersion's single source of truth: the gradle plugin
        # bundled with the SDK flutter-action installed. app/
        # build.gradle.kts reads `ndkVersion = flutter.ndkVersion`, so
        # resolving here can never skew from what AGP requests at
        # configuration time (a literal pin on either side would break
        # that coupling — the guard test pins both sides).
        if [ -n "${FLUTTER_ROOT:-}" ]; then
          FLUTTER_HOME="$FLUTTER_ROOT"
        else
          FLUTTER_BIN="$(command -v flutter || true)"
          if [ -z "$FLUTTER_BIN" ]; then
            echo "::error::cannot locate flutter (set FLUTTER_ROOT) — the NDK pre-install resolves the version from the SDK's gradle plugin source"
            exit 1
          fi
          FLUTTER_HOME="$(dirname "$(dirname "$FLUTTER_BIN")")"
        fi
        GRADLE_SRC="$FLUTTER_HOME/packages/flutter_tools/gradle/src/main/kotlin/FlutterExtension.kt"
        NDK_VERSION="$(grep -hoE 'val ndkVersion: String = "[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+"' "$GRADLE_SRC" 2>/dev/null | grep -oE '[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+' | head -1 || true)"
        if [ -z "$NDK_VERSION" ]; then
          echo "::error::cannot resolve flutter.ndkVersion from $GRADLE_SRC — the Flutter gradle plugin layout moved; update the extraction in .github/actions/android-ndk-preinstall (and test/ci_android_ndk_preinstall_guard_test.dart) TOGETHER"
          exit 1
        fi
        echo "resolved flutter.ndkVersion = $NDK_VERSION"
        ANDROID_SDK="${ANDROID_HOME:-/usr/local/lib/android/sdk}"
        SDKMANAGER="$ANDROID_SDK/cmdline-tools/latest/bin/sdkmanager"
        if [ ! -x "$SDKMANAGER" ]; then
          SDKMANAGER="$(command -v sdkmanager || true)"
        fi
        if [ -z "$SDKMANAGER" ]; then
          echo "::error::sdkmanager not found (expected $ANDROID_SDK/cmdline-tools/latest/bin/sdkmanager) — the NDK pre-install needs the Android cmdline-tools"
          exit 1
        fi
        # Idempotence: AGP resolves `ndkVersion` against
        # $ANDROID_HOME/ndk/<version> — source.properties present means
        # the NDK is fully installed; skip the download entirely.
        if [ -f "$ANDROID_SDK/ndk/$NDK_VERSION/source.properties" ]; then
          echo "NDK $NDK_VERSION already installed — skipping pre-install"
          exit 0
        fi
        # Accept any license the image has not pre-accepted so the
        # installs below never prompt (|| true: `yes` dies of SIGPIPE by
        # design once sdkmanager stops reading).
        yes | "$SDKMANAGER" --licenses > /dev/null || true
        # gh-1655: Gradle's own auto-install (the same sdkmanager call,
        # run inside configuration) has no retry — one truncated download
        # unzips as "Error on ZipFile unknown archive" and the build dies.
        # Here the same download gets three attempts with backoff.
        for attempt in 1 2 3; do
          echo "installing NDK $NDK_VERSION (attempt $attempt/3)"
          rm -rf "$ANDROID_SDK/ndk/$NDK_VERSION"
          if "$SDKMANAGER" --install "ndk;$NDK_VERSION"; then
            echo "NDK $NDK_VERSION installed"
            exit 0
          fi
          echo "::warning::sdkmanager NDK install failed (attempt $attempt/3) — retrying in 10s"
          sleep 10
        done
        echo "::error::NDK $NDK_VERSION install failed after 3 attempts — gh-1655 red'd the leg on a single truncated archive; inspect the sdkmanager output above"
        exit 1

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`

{"content":"🚨 **BLOCKING: re-send matcher swallows the opening frame of a second same-name tool call on clean relays (C4/AC3 regression)**

`_matchResentToolCallBlock` is consulted **unconditionally** — `resent ?? _lookupToolCallBlock(...)` means a matcher hit overrides the id/index identity lookup — and its merge condition treats "last block still has empty `partialArgs`" as mergeable. The PR description claims "Merge fires only on an id/index lookup miss — clean relays are unaffected by construction", but the code never checks the lookup, and the ticket's own spec ("when lookup misses **and** the incoming frame has no usable identity match") is not implemented.

**Demonstrated regression** (standard OpenAI-style stream: two parallel same-name calls whose opening frames carry `arguments: ""` — the normal shape; verified with a probe test: **fails on this head, passes on `origin/main`**):

```
chunk1: [{index:0, id:"call_a", function:{name:"bash", arguments:""}}]
chunk2: [{index:1, id:"call_b", function:{name:"bash", arguments:""}}]   ← swallowed
chunk3: [{index:0, function:{arguments:"{\"command\":\"ls\"}"}}]
chunk4: [{index:1, function:{arguments:"{\"command\":\"pwd\"}"}}]        ← creates a nameless/idless block
```

Result on this head: call 2 ends with `id: ""` **and** `name: ""` (unresolvable tool downstream). At the moment call B's opening frame arrives, the last block (A) has empty `partialArgs`, the names match, so `existing.isNotEmpty && !args.startsWith(existing)` is skipped and the frame merges into A — `toolCallBlocksById["call_b"]` is even rebound to A, and index 1 stays unbound, so the later fragment spawns a fresh block with no identity. This violates AC3/C4 ("no behavior change for clean relays"). Secondary hazard of the same ordering bug: a re-sent frame belonging to an *earlier* same-name block (its id/index lookup would HIT) is merged into the *last* block instead, corrupting that block's args.

**Fix** (keeps both new fixtures green):
1. Only consult the matcher when `_lookupToolCallBlock(streamIndex, id)` misses;
2. Require `existing.isNotEmpty` in the matcher — an empty `partialArgs` cannot distinguish "awaiting first fragment" from "genuinely new call".

Also add the missing C3d regression case: two same-name calls with standard empty-args openings (the current C3d test gives call B complete args, which is exactly the shape that dodges the hole).

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: the 1-char trim also eats legitimate single-char continuations, not only punctuation stutters**

The new `k >= 1` floor trims **any** leading single char equal to the current tail, and the ellipsis guard only fires when the same char repeats *inside* the delta (`delta.length > 1`). So on a clean relay that happens to split tokens as single characters, real text is destroyed:

- `'soo'` + `'o'` → `'soo'` (lost an `o`)
- `'wow'` + `'!'` + `'!'` → `'wow!'`
- `'yes'` + `'s'` + `'s'` → `'yes'`

All the gh-1655 evidence stutters are sentence punctuation (`. , : ; ? !`), and the ticket's C1 concern is exactly that class. Consider restricting the 1-char trim to punctuation-only leading chars (e.g. `const oneCharStutter = '.',',':';'?';!'.contains(delta[0])`) — that keeps the fix targeted at the observed relay defect and makes doubled/tripled letters safe by construction. If you keep the unrestricted trim, at least pin the accepted tradeoff in the doc comment so a future reader doesn't mistake it for a bug.

- `_matchResentToolCallBlock`: no tool-call block yet → last=null → null.
- `_ensureToolCallBlock`: lookup(0, 'call_a') → miss → create A. partialArgs = '{"command":"ls"}'.

Frame 2 (second identical call): `{index: 1, id: 'call_b', function: {name: 'bash', arguments: '{"command":"ls"}'}}`.

- `_ensureToolCallBlock`: block = A (resend wins over lookup → lookup(1,'call_b') never consulted → miss not detected).
- `_applyToolCallIdentity(A, frame2)`: A.id is non-empty ('call_a'), so id NOT adopted. A.name non-empty → not updated.
- toolDelta = '{"command":"ls"}', resend != null → existing = '{"command":"ls"}', startsWith → toolDelta = '' → return.
- Result: ONE block. The second identical call is silently swallowed. ToolCallStartEvent for it never fires; index 1/id 'call_b' never registered.

This confirms: a clean relay emitting two identical calls in one message now produces ONE call. This violates C4/AC3 ("no behavior change for clean relays... byte-identical output") and is a real correctness regression (silent dropped tool call). And it contradicts the PR description's claim "Merge fires only on an id/index lookup miss — clean relays are unaffected by construction."

The ticket spec says the resend check should happen "when lookup misses and the incoming frame has no usable identity match". The implementation inverted the order: matcher first, identity lookup second. The fix would be to consult `_matchResentToolCallBlock` only when `_lookupToolCallBlock(streamIndex, id)` misses (and arguably only when the frame carries a genuinely new id with no matching index — per ticket: "a frame whose name equals..." — the PR description itself says "on a lookup miss").

Re-sent frame with fresh id `call_b` and NO index: lookup(null, 'call_b') → toolCallBlocksById['call_b'] → miss (new id never seen) → then matcher → merge. ✓. Re-sent frame with fresh id AND an index (some relays resend with index): the ticket says "carrying a NEW relay-generated id and no (or another) index". Two identical tool calls in one message: e.g., a model calling `read` twice on the same file with identical args (common when the model wants fresh content — actually identical parallel reads happen), or two identical `grep` calls, or web_search with the same query twice. Models do this occasionally, especially in parallel-tool-call mode. The result: one call silently dropped. This is a correctness bug on clean relays introduced by this PR — exactly the class of regression AC3/C4 was written to prevent. Severity: BLOCKING.

blocks.text:
name: android-ndk-preinstall
description: >-
  Pre-install the Flutter-pinned Android NDK so Gradle configuration never
  triggers an on-demand sdkmanager download mid-build. gh-1655: one
  truncated android-ndk-r28c-linux download ("Error on ZipFile unknown
  archive" at 33%) red'd the ci.yml build-android leg — and the aggregate
  Quality gate with it — because AGP's in-configuration auto-install path
  has NO retry. The NDK version is resolved from the pinned Flutter SDK's
  own gradle plugin source (the exact value flutter.ndkVersion resolves
  to — no second pin to drift), the install is skipped when the NDK is
  already present, and the download itself is bounded-retried — the same
  hardening the flutter_gemma Android seed carries (gh-1468). Companion
  guard: test/ci_android_ndk_preinstall_guard_test.dart.
runs:
  using: composite
  steps:
    - name: Pre-install the Flutter-pinned Android NDK (bounded retry)
      shell: bash
      run: |
        set -euo pipefail
        # flutter.ndkVersion's single source of truth: the gradle plugin
        # bundled with the SDK flutter-action installed. app/
        # build.gradle.kts reads `ndkVersion = flutter.ndkVersion`, so
        # resolving here can never skew from what AGP requests at
        # configuration time (a literal pin on either side would break
        # that coupling — the guard test pins both sides).
        if [ -n "${FLUTTER_ROOT:-}" ]; then
          FLUTTER_HOME="$FLUTTER_ROOT"
        else
          FLUTTER_BIN="$(command -v flutter || true)"
          if [ -z "$FLUTTER_BIN" ]; then
            echo "::error::cannot locate flutter (set FLUTTER_ROOT) — the NDK pre-install resolves the version from the SDK's gradle plugin source"
            exit 1
          fi
          FLUTTER_HOME="$(dirname "$(dirname "$FLUTTER_BIN")")"
        fi
        GRADLE_SRC="$FLUTTER_HOME/packages/flutter_tools/gradle/src/main/kotlin/FlutterExtension.kt"
        NDK_VERSION="$(grep -hoE 'val ndkVersion: String = "[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+"' "$GRADLE_SRC" 2>/dev/null | grep -oE '[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+' | head -1 || true)"
        if [ -z "$NDK_VERSION" ]; then
          echo "::error::cannot resolve flutter.ndkVersion from $GRADLE_SRC — the Flutter gradle plugin layout moved; update the extraction in .github/actions/android-ndk-preinstall (and test/ci_android_ndk_preinstall_guard_test.dart) TOGETHER"
          exit 1
        fi
        echo "resolved flutter.ndkVersion = $NDK_VERSION"
        ANDROID_SDK="${ANDROID_HOME:-/usr/local/lib/android/sdk}"
        SDKMANAGER="$ANDROID_SDK/cmdline-tools/latest/bin/sdkmanager"
        if [ ! -x "$SDKMANAGER" ]; then
          SDKMANAGER="$(command -v sdkmanager || true)"
        fi
        if [ -z "$SDKMANAGER" ]; then
          echo "::error::sdkmanager not found (expected $ANDROID_SDK/cmdline-tools/latest/bin/sdkmanager) — the NDK pre-install needs the Android cmdline-tools"
          exit 1
        fi
        # Idempotence: AGP resolves `ndkVersion` against
        # $ANDROID_HOME/ndk/<version> — source.properties present means
        # the NDK is fully installed; skip the download entirely.
        if [ -f "$ANDROID_SDK/ndk/$NDK_VERSION/source.properties" ]; then
          echo "NDK $NDK_VERSION already installed — skipping pre-install"
          exit 0
        fi
        # Accept any license the image has not pre-accepted so the
        # installs below never prompt (|| true: `yes` dies of SIGPIPE by
        # design once sdkmanager stops reading).
        yes | "$SDKMANAGER" --licenses > /dev/null || true
        # gh-1655: Gradle's own auto-install (the same sdkmanager call,
        # run inside configuration) has no retry — one truncated download
        # unzips as "Error on ZipFile unknown archive" and the build dies.
        # Here the same download gets three attempts with backoff.
        for attempt in 1 2 3; do
          echo "installing NDK $NDK_VERSION (attempt $attempt/3)"
          rm -rf "$ANDROID_SDK/ndk/$NDK_VERSION"
          if "$SDKMANAGER" --install "ndk;$NDK_VERSION"; then
            echo "NDK $NDK_VERSION installed"
            exit 0
          fi
          echo "::warning::sdkmanager NDK install failed (attempt $attempt/3) — retrying in 10s"
          sleep 10
        done
        echo "::error::NDK $NDK_VERSION install failed after 3 attempts — gh-1655 red'd the leg on a single truncated archive; inspect the sdkmanager output above"
        exit 1

Scenario B (re-sent frame for a non-last block with same name + prefix-args): lookup would hit the right block (index 0 → A), but the impl merges into B (last). Let me construct a concrete harmful case for the impl-vs-spec deviation that is REALISTIC:

A stuttering relay re-sends frames — that's the whole premise. Evidence shows the relay re-sent a tool-call frame with a fresh id. # AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`

{"content":"🚨 **BLOCKING: re-send matcher swallows the opening frame of a second same-name tool call on clean relays (C4/AC3 regression)**

`_matchResentToolCallBlock` is consulted **unconditionally** — `resent ?? _lookupToolCallBlock(...)` means a matcher hit overrides the id/index identity lookup — and its merge condition treats "last block still has empty `partialArgs`" as mergeable. The PR description claims "Merge fires only on an id/index lookup miss — clean relays are unaffected by construction", but the code never checks the lookup, and the ticket's own spec ("when lookup misses **and** the incoming frame has no usable identity match") is not implemented.

**Demonstrated regression** (standard OpenAI-style stream: two parallel same-name calls whose opening frames carry `arguments: ""` — the normal shape; verified with a probe test: **fails on this head, passes on `origin/main`**):

```
chunk1: [{index:0, id:"call_a", function:{name:"bash", arguments:""}}]
chunk2: [{index:1, id:"call_b", function:{name:"bash", arguments:""}}]   ← swallowed
chunk3: [{index:0, function:{arguments:"{\"command\":\"ls\"}"}}]
chunk4: [{index:1, function:{arguments:"{\"command\":\"pwd\"}"}}]        ← creates a nameless/idless block
```

Result on this head: call 2 ends with `id: ""` **and** `name: ""` (unresolvable tool downstream). At the moment call B's opening frame arrives, the last block (A) has empty `partialArgs`, the names match, so `existing.isNotEmpty && !args.startsWith(existing)` is skipped and the frame merges into A — `toolCallBlocksById["call_b"]` is even rebound to A, and index 1 stays unbound, so the later fragment spawns a fresh block with no identity. This violates AC3/C4 ("no behavior change for clean relays"). Secondary hazard of the same ordering bug: a re-sent frame belonging to an *earlier* same-name block (its id/index lookup would HIT) is merged into the *last* block instead, corrupting that block's args.

**Fix** (keeps both new fixtures green):
1. Only consult the matcher when `_lookupToolCallBlock(streamIndex, id)` misses;
2. Require `existing.isNotEmpty` in the matcher — an empty `partialArgs` cannot distinguish "awaiting first fragment" from "genuinely new call".

Also add the missing C3d regression case: two same-name calls with standard empty-args openings (the current C3d test gives call B complete args, which is exactly the shape that dodges the hole).

**Scenario A — two genuinely identical consecutive tool calls on a CLEAN relay:**

Frame 1: `{index: 0, id: 'call_a', function: {name: 'bash', arguments: '{"command":"ls"}'}}` (complete args in one frame).
- `_matchResentToolCallBlock`: no tool-call block yet → last=null → null.
- `_ensureToolCallBlock`: lookup(0, 'call_a') → miss → create A. partialArgs = '{"command":"ls"}'.

Frame 2 (second identical call): `{index: 1, id: 'call_b', function: {name: 'bash', arguments: '{"command":"ls"}'}}`.

- `_ensureToolCallBlock`: block = A (resend wins over lookup → lookup(1,'call_b') never consulted → miss not detected).
- `_applyToolCallIdentity(A, frame2)`: A.id is non-empty ('call_a'), so id NOT adopted. A.name non-empty → not updated.
- toolDelta = '{"command":"ls"}', resend != null → existing = '{"command":"ls"}', startsWith → toolDelta = '' → return.
- Result: ONE block. The second identical call is silently swallowed. ToolCallStartEvent for it never fires; index 1/id 'call_b' never registered.

This confirms: a clean relay emitting two identical calls in one message now produces ONE call. This violates C4/AC3 ("no behavior change for clean relays... byte-identical output") and is a real correctness regression (silent dropped tool call). And it contradicts the PR description's claim "Merge fires only on an id/index lookup miss — clean relays are unaffected by construction."

The ticket spec says the resend check should happen "when lookup misses and the incoming frame has no usable identity match". The implementation inverted the order: matcher first, identity lookup second. The fix would be to consult `_matchResentToolCallBlock` only when `_lookupToolCallBlock(streamIndex, id)` misses (and arguably only when the frame carries a genuinely new id with no matching index — per ticket: "a frame whose name equals..." — the PR description itself says "on a lookup miss").

Wait, but let me be careful — could checking "lookup miss first" break the actual stutter-resend case? Re-sent frame with fresh id `call_b` and NO index: lookup(null, 'call_b') → toolCallBlocksById['call_b'] → miss (new id never seen) → then matcher → merge. ✓. Re-sent frame with fresh id AND an index (some relays resend with index): the ticket says "carrying a NEW relay-generated id and no (or another) index". If it carried the SAME index → lookup hits → merge via normal path. If it carries ANOTHER index → lookup misses → matcher fires → merge (but then the streamIndex registration: block.streamIndex != null (0) so not overwritten; `toolCallBlocksByIndex[1] = A`? No — the `if (streamIndex != null && block.streamIndex == null)` guard prevents rebinding index 1 to A. Hmm, but then future frames with index 1 would create a new block... messy but that's the stutter case).

So the correct ordering (lookup first, matcher on miss) would fix Scenario A while still fixing the bug. The current implementation is a deviation from the ticket's specified fix.

Is Scenario A realistic enough for BLOCKING? Two identical tool calls in one message: e.g., a model calling `read` twice on the same file with identical args (common when the model wants fresh content — actually identical parallel reads happen), or two identical `grep` calls, or web_search with the same query twice. Models do this occasionally, especially in parallel-tool-call mode. The result: one call silently dropped. This is a correctness bug on clean relays introduced by this PR — exactly the class of regression AC3/C4 was written to prevent. Severity: BLOCKING.

**Scenario B — named frame for a non-last block (stutter relay resending an earlier frame after a newer block started):**

A (index 0, bash) done; B (index 1, bash) streaming with partialArgs '{"comma'. A re-sent A frame arrives: `{index: 0, function: {name: 'bash', arguments: '{"command":"ls"}'}}`. 
- matcher: name bash == last B.name bash; existing='{"comma'; args='{"command":"ls"}'.startsWith('{"comma') → TRUE → match returns B (the WRONG block).
- `_ensureToolCallBlock`: block = B. Lookup would have routed by index 0 → A. Instead the frame merges into B: toolDelta='{"command":"ls"}' minus prefix '{"comma' → 'nd":"ls"}' appended to B → B.args = '{"command":"ls"}' — corrupted; A loses its resend (fine, A was complete anyway).

Hmm wait — actually in this scenario, would a lookup by index 0 have hit A? Yes: toolCallBlocksByIndex[0] = A. So the correct order (lookup first) would route to A, then `resend`-less append: toolDelta='{"command":"ls"}' appended to A's args → A.args doubled ('{"command":"ls"}{"command":"ls"}')! Hmm, so lookup-first alone doesn't fix the stutter for re-sent COMPLETE frames against completed blocks — the suffix trim is keyed on `resend != null`. But wait — if lookup HITS (same index 0), that's the same-id same-index re-send case: the PR's fix as written doesn't trim there either (resend matcher only helps when matched). Actually if lookup hits A and the frame is a full re-send of A's args, old behavior: args doubled. New behavior with lookup-first: still doubled (no trim). Hmm.

name: android-ndk-preinstall
description: >-
  Pre-install the Flutter-pinned Android NDK so Gradle configuration never
  triggers an on-demand sdkmanager download mid-build. gh-1655: one
  truncated android-ndk-r28c-linux download ("Error on ZipFile unknown
  archive" at 33%) red'd the ci.yml build-android leg — and the aggregate
  Quality gate with it — because AGP's in-configuration auto-install path
  has NO retry. The NDK version is resolved from the pinned Flutter SDK's
  own gradle plugin source (the exact value flutter.ndkVersion resolves
  to — no second pin to drift), the install is skipped when the NDK is
  already present, and the download itself is bounded-retried — the same
  hardening the flutter_gemma Android seed carries (gh-1468). Companion
  guard: test/ci_android_ndk_preinstall_guard_test.dart.
runs:
  using: composite
  steps:
    - name: Pre-install the Flutter-pinned Android NDK (bounded retry)
      shell: bash
      run: |
        set -euo pipefail
        # flutter.ndkVersion's single source of truth: the gradle plugin
        # bundled with the SDK flutter-action installed. app/
        # build.gradle.kts reads `ndkVersion = flutter.ndkVersion`, so
        # resolving here can never skew from what AGP requests at
        # configuration time (a literal pin on either side would break
        # that coupling — the guard test pins both sides).
        if [ -n "${FLUTTER_ROOT:-}" ]; then
          FLUTTER_HOME="$FLUTTER_ROOT"
        else
          FLUTTER_BIN="$(command -v flutter || true)"
          if [ -z "$FLUTTER_BIN" ]; then
            echo "::error::cannot locate flutter (set FLUTTER_ROOT) — the NDK pre-install resolves the version from the SDK's gradle plugin source"
            exit 1
          fi
          FLUTTER_HOME="$(dirname "$(dirname "$FLUTTER_BIN")")"
        fi
        GRADLE_SRC="$FLUTTER_HOME/packages/flutter_tools/gradle/src/main/kotlin/FlutterExtension.kt"
        NDK_VERSION="$(grep -hoE 'val ndkVersion: String = "[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+"' "$GRADLE_SRC" 2>/dev/null | grep -oE '[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+' | head -1 || true)"
        if [ -z "$NDK_VERSION" ]; then
          echo "::error::cannot resolve flutter.ndkVersion from $GRADLE_SRC — the Flutter gradle plugin layout moved; update the extraction in .github/actions/android-ndk-preinstall (and test/ci_android_ndk_preinstall_guard_test.dart) TOGETHER"
          exit 1
        fi
        echo "resolved flutter.ndkVersion = $NDK_VERSION"
        ANDROID_SDK="${ANDROID_HOME:-/usr/local/lib/android/sdk}"
        SDKMANAGER="$ANDROID_SDK/cmdline-tools/latest/bin/sdkmanager"
        if [ ! -x "$SDKMANAGER" ]; then
          SDKMANAGER="$(command -v sdkmanager || true)"
        fi
        if [ -z "$SDKMANAGER" ]; then
          echo "::error::sdkmanager not found (expected $ANDROID_SDK/cmdline-tools/latest/bin/sdkmanager) — the NDK pre-install needs the Android cmdline-tools"
          exit 1
        fi
        # Idempotence: AGP resolves `ndkVersion` against
        # $ANDROID_HOME/ndk/<version> — source.properties present means
        # the NDK is fully installed; skip the download entirely.
        if [ -f "$ANDROID_SDK/ndk/$NDK_VERSION/source.properties" ]; then
          echo "NDK $NDK_VERSION already installed — skipping pre-install"
          exit 0
        fi
        # Accept any license the image has not pre-accepted so the
        # installs below never prompt (|| true: `yes` dies of SIGPIPE by
        # design once sdkmanager stops reading).
        yes | "$SDKMANAGER" --licenses > /dev/null || true
        # gh-1655: Gradle's own auto-install (the same sdkmanager call,
        # run inside configuration) has no retry — one truncated download
        # unzips as "Error on ZipFile unknown archive" and the build dies.
        # Here the same download gets three attempts with backoff.
        for attempt in 1 2 3; do
          echo "installing NDK $NDK_VERSION (attempt $attempt/3)"
          rm -rf "$ANDROID_SDK/ndk/$NDK_VERSION"
          if "$SDKMANAGER" --install "ndk;$NDK_VERSION"; then
            echo "NDK $NDK_VERSION installed"
            exit 0
          fi
          echo "::warning::sdkmanager NDK install failed (attempt $attempt/3) — retrying in 10s"
          sleep 10
        done
        echo "::error::NDK $NDK_VERSION install failed after 3 attempts — gh-1655 red'd the leg on a single truncated archive; inspect the sdkmanager output above"
        exit 1

Anchor: the `final resend = _matchResentToolCallBlock(rawToolCall);` line or the `resent ?? _lookupToolCallBlock` line in the diff. Wait — careful: requiring `existing.isNotEmpty` would break the PR's own C3c test? Let me check: re-sent frame with fresh id, args FULL '{"command":"js hello.js"}', existing after frame 1 = '{"command":"js hello.js"}' — non-empty → still merges. Good, C3c survives. The re-send case in the wild (evidence) had the block's args fully accumulated → existing non-empty → merge works. So the minimal fix (`existing.isNotEmpty` + lookup-miss gating) preserves the PR's goals and fixes the regression. I'll propose exactly that.

Also check: does the early-return `if (toolDelta.isEmpty) return;` skip the `ToolCallDeltaEvent` — for a swallowed-duplicate frame that's fine.

2. **Matcher bypasses identity lookup on hit (deviation from ticket spec)** — Scenario B: a re-sent frame for a non-last block with same name and prefix-matching args merges into the WRONG block, corrupting args. The ticket says the resend check applies only "when lookup misses and the incoming frame has no usable identity match"; the impl applies it always (`resent ?? lookup`). It's really the same root cause as BLOCKING 1 — I'll fold it into the same comment (root cause + both symptoms), keeping one blocking finding. Cleaner.

Then '.' appended (text 'wait' doesn't end with '.'). "wait." then " I should". Fine. Legit double punctuation like "?!" split: "really" + "?" + "!" → 'really?!' — second delta '!' — text ends with '?' not '!' → appended ✓. Legit "!!" as separate deltas: "wow" + "!" + "!" → second '!' trimmed → 'wow!' — data loss on clean relay! "Hello!!" is real text. But same accepted tradeoff class as ticket C1. # AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`

{"content":"🚨 **BLOCKING: re-send matcher swallows the opening frame of a second same-name tool call on clean relays (C4/AC3 regression)**

`_matchResentToolCallBlock` is consulted **unconditionally** — `resent ?? _lookupToolCallBlock(...)` means a matcher hit overrides the id/index identity lookup — and its merge condition treats "last block still has empty `partialArgs`" as mergeable. The PR description claims "Merge fires only on an id/index lookup miss — clean relays are unaffected by construction", but the code never checks the lookup, and the ticket's own spec ("when lookup misses **and** the incoming frame has no usable identity match") is not implemented.

**Demonstrated regression** (standard OpenAI-style stream: two parallel same-name calls whose opening frames carry `arguments: ""` — the normal shape; verified with a probe test: **fails on this head, passes on `origin/main`**):

```
chunk1: [{index:0, id:"call_a", function:{name:"bash", arguments:""}}]
chunk2: [{index:1, id:"call_b", function:{name:"bash", arguments:""}}]   ← swallowed
chunk3: [{index:0, function:{arguments:"{\"command\":\"ls\"}"}}]
chunk4: [{index:1, function:{arguments:"{\"command\":\"pwd\"}"}}]        ← creates a nameless/idless block
```

Result on this head: call 2 ends with `id: ""` **and** `name: ""` (unresolvable tool downstream). At the moment call B's opening frame arrives, the last block (A) has empty `partialArgs`, the names match, so `existing.isNotEmpty && !args.startsWith(existing)` is skipped and the frame merges into A — `toolCallBlocksById["call_b"]` is even rebound to A, and index 1 stays unbound, so the later fragment spawns a fresh block with no identity. This violates AC3/C4 ("no behavior change for clean relays"). Secondary hazard of the same ordering bug: a re-sent frame belonging to an *earlier* same-name block (its id/index lookup would HIT) is merged into the *last* block instead, corrupting that block's args.

**Fix** (keeps both new fixtures green):
1. Only consult the matcher when `_lookupToolCallBlock(streamIndex, id)` misses;
2. Require `existing.isNotEmpty` in the matcher — an empty `partialArgs` cannot distinguish "awaiting first fragment" from "genuinely new call".

Also add the missing C3d regression case: two same-name calls with standard empty-args openings (the current C3d test gives call B complete args, which is exactly the shape that dodges the hole).

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: the 1-char trim also eats legitimate single-char continuations, not only punctuation stutters**

The new `k >= 1` floor trims **any** leading single char equal to the current tail, and the ellipsis guard only fires when the same char repeats *inside* the delta (`delta.length > 1`). So on a clean relay that happens to split tokens as single characters, real text is destroyed:

- `'soo'` + `'o'` → `'soo'` (lost an `o`)
- `'wow'` + `'!'` + `'!'` → `'wow!'`
- `'yes'` + `'s'` + `'s'` → `'yes'`

All the gh-1655 evidence stutters are sentence punctuation (`. , : ; ? !`), and the ticket's C1 concern is exactly that class. Consider restricting the 1-char trim to punctuation-only leading chars (e.g. `const oneCharStutter = '.',',':';'?';!'.contains(delta[0])`) — that keeps the fix targeted at the observed relay defect and makes doubled/tripled letters safe by construction. If you keep the unrestricted trim, at least pin the accepted tradeoff in the doc comment so a future reader doesn't mistake it for a bug.

After attempt 3 fails, the loop still emits `::warning:: ... retrying in 10s` and sleeps — then falls out of the loop and exits 1. That logs a false "retrying" warning and wastes 10s of a paid runner before the `::error::` fires:

```bash
for attempt in 1 2 3; do
  echo "installing NDK $NDK_VERSION (attempt $attempt/3)"
  rm -rf "$ANDROID_SDK/ndk/$NDK_VERSION"
  if "$SDKMANAGER" --install "ndk;$NDK_VERSION"; then
    echo "NDK $NDK_VERSION installed"
    exit 0
  fi
  if [ "$attempt" -lt 3 ]; then
    echo "::warning::sdkmanager NDK install failed (attempt $attempt/3) — retrying in 10s"
    sleep 10
  fi
done

Now I've confirmed the key concern. Let me trace through the critical false-positive scenarios:

**Scenario A — two genuinely identical consecutive tool calls on a CLEAN relay:**

Frame 1: `{index: 0, id: 'call_a', function: {name: 'bash', arguments: '{"command":"ls"}'}}` (complete args in one frame).
- `_matchResentToolCallBlock`: no tool-call block yet → last=null → null.
- `_ensureToolCallBlock`: lookup(0, 'call_a') → miss → create A. partialArgs = '{"command":"ls"}'.

Frame 2 (second identical call): `{index: 1, id: 'call_b', function: {name: 'bash', arguments: '{"command":"ls"}'}}`.
- `_matchResentToolCallBlock`: name='bash', last=A, A.name='bash' match. existing='{"command":"ls"}'. args='{"command":"ls"}'. `existing.isNotEmpty && !args.startsWith(existing)` → args DOES start with existing (identical) → returns A!
- `_ensureToolCallBlock`: block = A (resend wins over lookup → lookup(1,'call_b') never consulted → miss not detected).
- `_applyToolCallIdentity(A, frame2)`: A.id is non-empty ('call_a'), so id NOT adopted. A.name non-empty → not updated.
- toolDelta = '{"command":"ls"}', resend != null → existing = '{"command":"ls"}', startsWith → toolDelta = '' → return.
- Result: ONE block. The second identical call is silently swallowed. ToolCallStartEvent for it never fires; index 1/id 'call_b' never registered.

This confirms: a clean relay emitting two identical calls in one message now produces ONE call. This violates C4/AC3 ("no behavior change for clean relays... byte-identical output") and is a real correctness regression (silent dropped tool call). And it contradicts the PR description's claim "Merge fires only on an id/index lookup miss — clean relays are unaffected by construction."

The ticket spec says the resend check should happen "when lookup misses and the incoming frame has no usable identity match". The implementation inverted the order: matcher first, identity lookup second. The fix would be to consult `_matchResentToolCallBlock` only when `_lookupToolCallBlock(streamIndex, id)` misses (and arguably only when the frame carries a genuinely new id with no matching index — per ticket: "a frame whose name equals..." — the PR description itself says "on a lookup miss").

Wait, but let me be careful — could checking "lookup miss first" break the actual stutter-resend case? Re-sent frame with fresh id `call_b` and NO index: lookup(null, 'call_b') → toolCallBlocksById['call_b'] → miss (new id never seen) → then matcher → merge. ✓. Re-sent frame with fresh id AND an index (some relays resend with index): the ticket says "carrying a NEW relay-generated id and no (or another) index". If it carried the SAME index → lookup hits → merge via normal path. If it carries ANOTHER index → lookup misses → matcher fires → merge (but then the streamIndex registration: block.streamIndex != null (0) so not overwritten; `toolCallBlocksByIndex[1] = A`? No — the `if (streamIndex != null && block.streamIndex == null)` guard prevents rebinding index 1 to A. Hmm, but then future frames with index 1 would create a new block... messy but that's the stutter case).

So the correct ordering (lookup first, matcher on miss) would fix Scenario A while still fixing the bug. The current implementation is a deviation from the ticket's specified fix.

Is Scenario A realistic enough for BLOCKING? Two identical tool calls in one message: e.g., a model calling `read` twice on the same file with identical args (common when the model wants fresh content — actually identical parallel reads happen), or two identical `grep` calls, or web_search with the same query twice. Models do this occasionally, especially in parallel-tool-call mode. The result: one call silently dropped. This is a correctness bug on clean relays introduced by this PR — exactly the class of regression AC3/C4 was written to prevent. Severity: BLOCKING.

**Scenario B — named frame for a non-last block (stutter relay resending an earlier frame after a newer block started):**

A (index 0, bash) done; B (index 1, bash) streaming with partialArgs '{"comma'. A re-sent A frame arrives: `{index: 0, function: {name: 'bash', arguments: '{"command":"ls"}'}}`. 
- matcher: name bash == last B.name bash; existing='{"comma'; args='{"command":"ls"}'.startsWith('{"comma') → TRUE → match returns B (the WRONG block).
- `_ensureToolCallBlock`: block = B. Lookup would have routed by index 0 → A. Instead the frame merges into B: toolDelta='{"command":"ls"}' minus prefix '{"comma' → 'nd":"ls"}' appended to B → B.args = '{"command":"ls"}' — corrupted; A loses its resend (fine, A was complete anyway).

Hmm wait — actually in this scenario, would a lookup by index 0 have hit A? Yes: toolCallBlocksByIndex[0] = A. So the correct order (lookup first) would route to A, then `resend`-less append: toolDelta='{"command":"ls"}' appended to A's args → A.args doubled ('{"command":"ls"}{"command":"ls"}')! Hmm, so lookup-first alone doesn't fix the stutter for re-sent COMPLETE frames against completed blocks — the suffix trim is keyed on `resend != null`. But wait — if lookup HITS (same index 0), that's the same-id same-index re-send case: the PR's fix as written doesn't trim there either (resend matcher only helps when matched). Actually if lookup hits A and the frame is a full re-send of A's args, old behavior: args doubled. New behavior with lookup-first: still doubled (no trim). Hmm.

But realistically: does the relay resend frames for block AFTER block B started? The JoinGonka evidence shows a re-sent frame with a FRESH id — i.e. the same call re-sent with a new id right around the same point. The evidence shows the re-send arrives while the call is the last one (both execute at the same startedAt). Scenario B is speculative; Scenario A is the concrete regression.

There's also **Scenario C — clean relay that repeats `name` on every continuation frame** (some providers do resend `function.name` with each args fragment):
- Frame 1: `{index:0, id:'a', name:'bash', args:'{"comm'}` → create A, partial '{"comm'.
- Frame 2: `{index:0, id:'a', name:'bash', args:'{"command":"ls"}'}` (cumulative style) → matcher: last=A, name match, existing='{"comm' prefix of args → resend=A; `_ensureToolCallBlock`: block=A — same as lookup. Trim → append 'and":"ls"}'. Fine, works.
- But INCREMENTAL style with repeated name: Frame 2: `{index:0, id:'a', name:'bash', args:'and":"ls"}'}` → matcher: existing='{"comm', args='and":"ls"}' — not startsWith → no match → lookup(0,'a') → A → append whole → correct. OK.

So Scenario C works. The problem cases are A (identical consecutive calls swallowed) and B (misrouting when matcher overrides identity).

Let me also double check **Scenario D — matcher fires when lookup would MISS but frame is genuinely new AND its args are empty**:
Frame: `{index:1, id:'call_b', function:{name:'bash', arguments:''}}` — genuinely new second call, but args empty string at start (OpenAI sends `arguments: ""` on the first frame sometimes!). matcher: last=A (bash), name match. existing='{"command":"ls"}' (A complete). args='' → `''`.startsWith(existing) false → no match. blocks.text:
name: android-ndk-preinstall
description: >-
  Pre-install the Flutter-pinned Android NDK so Gradle configuration never
  triggers an on-demand sdkmanager download mid-build. gh-1655: one
  truncated android-ndk-r28c-linux download ("Error on ZipFile unknown
  archive" at 33%) red'd the ci.yml build-android leg — and the aggregate
  Quality gate with it — because AGP's in-configuration auto-install path
  has NO retry. The NDK version is resolved from the pinned Flutter SDK's
  own gradle plugin source (the exact value flutter.ndkVersion resolves
  to — no second pin to drift), the install is skipped when the NDK is
  already present, and the download itself is bounded-retried — the same
  hardening the flutter_gemma Android seed carries (gh-1468). Companion
  guard: test/ci_android_ndk_preinstall_guard_test.dart.
runs:
  using: composite
  steps:
    - name: Pre-install the Flutter-pinned Android NDK (bounded retry)
      shell: bash
      run: |
        set -euo pipefail
        # flutter.ndkVersion's single source of truth: the gradle plugin
        # bundled with the SDK flutter-action installed. app/
        # build.gradle.kts reads `ndkVersion = flutter.ndkVersion`, so
        # resolving here can never skew from what AGP requests at
        # configuration time (a literal pin on either side would break
        # that coupling — the guard test pins both sides).
        if [ -n "${FLUTTER_ROOT:-}" ]; then
          FLUTTER_HOME="$FLUTTER_ROOT"
        else
          FLUTTER_BIN="$(command -v flutter || true)"
          if [ -z "$FLUTTER_BIN" ]; then
            echo "::error::cannot locate flutter (set FLUTTER_ROOT) — the NDK pre-install resolves the version from the SDK's gradle plugin source"
            exit 1
          fi
          FLUTTER_HOME="$(dirname "$(dirname "$FLUTTER_BIN")")"
        fi
        GRADLE_SRC="$FLUTTER_HOME/packages/flutter_tools/gradle/src/main/kotlin/FlutterExtension.kt"

        # Idempotence: AGP resolves `ndkVersion` against

        if [ -f "$ANDROID_SDK/ndk/$NDK_VERSION/source.properties" ]; then

          exit 0
        fi
        # Accept any license the image has not pre-accepted so the
        # installs below never prompt (|| true: `yes` dies of SIGPIPE by

        # unzips as "Error on ZipFile unknown archive" and the build dies.
        # Here the same download gets three attempts with backoff.
        for attempt in 1 2 3; do

          if "$SDKMANAGER" --install "ndk;$NDK_VERSION"; then
            echo "NDK $NDK_VERSION installed"
            exit 0
          fi
          echo "::warning::sdkmanager NDK install failed (attempt $attempt/3) — retrying in 10s"
          sleep 10
        done
        echo "::error::NDK $NDK_VERSION install failed after 3 attempts — gh-1655 red'd the leg on a single truncated archive; inspect the sdkmanager output above"

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`

`_matchResentToolCallBlock` is consulted **unconditionally** — `resent ?? _lookupToolCallBlock(...)` means a matcher hit overrides the id/index identity lookup — and its merge condition treats "last block still has empty `partialArgs`" as mergeable. The PR description claims "Merge fires only on an id/index lookup miss — clean relays are unaffected by construction", but the code never checks the lookup, and the ticket's own spec ("when lookup misses **and** the incoming frame has no usable identity match") is not implemented.

**Demonstrated regression** (standard OpenAI-style stream: two parallel same-name calls whose opening frames carry `arguments: ""` — the normal shape; verified with a probe test: **fails on this head, passes on `origin/main`**):

```

chunk2: [{index:1, id:"call_b", function:{name:"bash", arguments:""}}]   ← swallowed

You are Fa, a coding agent (also called fa). Never refer to yourself as pi, Claude, or any other assistant name. You help with software engineering tasks in the working directory /home/runner/work/flutter_agent_harness/flutter_agent_harness. Use the read, write, ls, and bash tools to inspect and modify files and run commands. Be concise.

## Session recall — never answer about the past from assumption

1. **Reference = search.** When the user references any past decision, rule, task, or artifact ("remember when…", "the rules we made", "that issue from last week"), call `session_search` BEFORE answering. Never answer about the past from assumption.
2. **Resume ritual.** After a compaction boundary is crossed or the session resumes, read the obligations ledger block (the `<system-notice>` titled "obligations ledger") first; it is the contract of what is still owed.
3. **Commit in the open.** Before promising a follow-up, check the ledger. When you arm a timer or watch (`schedule_message`), state the reason clearly in the message text — the engine writes a `pending-wait` ledger entry from it, and the fired timer re-enters a context that knows why it exists.
4. **Durable ≠ session.** Cross-session rules go to long-term memory immediately (`memory_add`); session-scoped obligations stay in the ledger. Never misuse either layer for the other.
5. **Dig idioms.** Markers are the TOC. `session_search` locates, `compact_expand` reads. `read $FAH_SESSION_FILE:<line>` is the zero-tool fallback.

## FinalizeGate — verify produced state before declaring done

You are running unattended: nobody re-checks your work after you declare it. **Trivial turns — answer directly:** when the turn made NO tool calls at all — no files written or edited, no commands run, nothing created or changed; a pure question answered from what you already know — there is nothing to verify. Skip the checklist AND the task ledger entirely and reply plainly; the gate exists for produced state, and with none the checklist is noise.

The contract does NOT apply to turns like:

- **"почему ты баш команды вызываешь?"** — a "why did you…" question. Just answer it directly: no checklist, no verification commands, no ledger.
- **"what does the `read` selector `:N` do?"** — a "what does X do" question. Just explain it: no verification commands, no ledger.
- **"what's the status?"** — a status/explanation answer about work already done. Report it plainly: no re-verification, no ledger.

Those turns produced no state; running the checklist ritual on them is noise. Otherwise, before ANY final summary you MUST:

1. **Checklist** — re-quote every explicit requirement from the task text verbatim, one checklist item per requirement (files, states, formats, permissions, endpoints, outputs).
2. **Verify each item with a real command** against the produced state — never from memory, never "I wrote it earlier". Note expected vs actual.
3. **Fix every unmet item** — a failed item is fixed and re-verified. Fix attempts are bounded: don't spiral on one dead end — switch approach.

**Work to the wall.** Your time-left notices report the remaining budget. While work remains, the next compliant action is another approach — not a final answer. Do not stop to wrap up: you are interrupted automatically when time expires, so no manual saving-up is needed. A final answer is written when the task is done or the deadline notice says so.

Named checks every checklist must include when they apply:

- **Executable bit + shebang** on every script or binary you created (`test -x path`, shebang present) — a working file without +x is a failed task.
- **Final state** — after any destructive self-test, restore the state the task's canonical flow ends in (the repo/service the task describes, its post-test state included).
- **Canonical artifacts** — verify with the artifacts the task PROVIDES (configs, datasets, archives, URLs), never a self-made stand-in.
- **Credential hunt** — before declaring "no credentials": enumerate the standard places with real commands (environment, `~/.aws/`, `~/.config/`, `~/.hf/`, `~/.git-credentials`, `~/.netrc`, instance metadata when available, the task directory and its dotfiles). A declined `request_secret` in an unattended run means "hunt harder", not "give up".
- **Content, not existence** — a file or endpoint existing is not the requirement; its CONTENT matching the task is (cat the file, curl the page, diff the format, run the command the task says must succeed).
- **Grader parity** — your shell is not the verifier's: a produced entry point (a script/CLI the grader will run) is verified only when it survives the grader's own invocation. Re-run each produced entry point from a different working directory (`cd /` — any neutral cwd, never the session cwd) in a fresh subprocess with a clean env (no session-exported vars), capture stdout, stderr and exit code, and diff against the earlier in-session run. Any divergence — different output, files created via relative paths now missing, locale/encoding-dependent output — is a `fail` ledger item, not a pass.

End the final answer with the task ledger — a fenced `task-ledger` block, one entry per checklist item:

```task-ledger
- requirement: <verbatim requirement quote>
  command: <the verification command you ran>
  expected: <what it should show>
  actual: <what it actually showed>
  status: pass|fixed|fail
```

`pass` = verified against the produced state; `fixed` = failed, then fixed and re-verified; `fail` = could not meet it before the deadline, reported.

## Agent messaging

You have an inbox in the session-shared messaging fabric. Your address is `01a1481c-98e3-75d8-8024-21db55e6e296/main`. Other Fa instances running in this project have their own inboxes — their orchestrators are reachable at `<theirSessionId>/main`, your subagents at their plain ids. Live instances also expose their session display name (`--session goal_builder`): `agent_directory` shows it next to the mailbox id, and `agent_message` accepts the name directly — `goal_builder` or `goal_builder/main` — so you rarely need the raw id. Use the `agent_directory` tool to list the live mailboxes (plus anything holding pending mail; pass `all: true` for long-dead ones and full mailbox ids — the default view truncates ids to save tokens) and `agent_message` to send. Each row also shows the last-activity time: `active 2m ago` means the watcher is live, `last active 3h ago (asleep)` means the process is gone. If you message an asleep target, the harness automatically launches a detached headless run of its session (`fa --session <name>`) to process the inbox; that run appends to the same session JSONL, so a later interactive start resumes the same conversation. Incoming mail is delivered to you automatically between turns (and wakes you when idle); reply with `agent_message` to the sender's address when a response is expected. Never guess mailbox addresses — read them from `agent_directory`.
When a hub is configured, `agent_directory` also lists hub peers beyond this project's file inboxes (embedded hosts, other machines) with their id and name — message them with `agent_message` the same way; the hub delivers even while a peer is offline (it drains when the peer reconnects).

Peers on OTHER machines are addressed `name@machine` (use a machine name you were told, or one from the peer itself): `agent_message to: "goal_builder@renderbox"` routes through the A2A gateway when this host's config has an `a2a.servers.renderbox` entry — delivery is synchronous there, so an error means the mail did NOT land (retry or tell the user).
